precepts.label: Exodus 13:3
precepts.why:
In Egypt the Lord told Moses and Aaron, “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you”. Jump to verse 11 to see what holiday comes in that month: “ye shall eat it in haste: it is the Lord’s passover”. So Passover comes in the first month. But what is the name of that first month?

Exodus 13 tells us: “And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten. This day came ye out in the month Abib”.

Abib, or Aviv, means spring: the season when the young, tender barley ears first appear. It marks the start of the year, the time of Passover and the firstfruits, renewal and freedom from Egypt. So the first month, the month of Passover, is the spring month. Not January.

That matters, because the months of the year are all from Rome. January is named for Janus, the Roman god of beginnings, and America, exercising all the power of the first beast, has the whole earth keeping Rome's new year. The Most High set the beginning of months in the spring, the month we came out of the house of bondage.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 16:1
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 16:1 is where Moses names the month again with the Passover. It joins the Passover and the month of Abib together, the same as Exodus 13, which says of the night we came out of Egypt, “This day came ye out in the month Abib”. The first month of Exodus 12:2, “the beginning of months”, is Abib, the spring month when the tender barley ears appear.

So the biblical new year does not begin in January. It begins in the spring, at Abib, and each month begins with the moon. January is from the Roman god Janus, who presided over doorways, time and new years.

Who changed it? Daniel 7:25 says the beast “shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws”. The great words are the lies Rome spoke against the Most High: a white man who died for the sins of everybody on the planet, that you must be dumped in the water to be saved, Lent, Christmas and December 25th. Wearing out the saints is the slavery. And changing times and laws is moving the beginning of the year from spring to January, and even daylight saving time. Keeping Abib is coming back to the Most High's times.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 3:16-17
precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses”. That is purging the old leaven. We had to do it physically, but it is something spiritual today. So what is your house today? “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” You, me, we are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God is to dwell in us because our temple was destroyed.

Look at how we purge leaven from the house. Brothers dump out the toaster, sweep underneath the floor mats and in the corners where stuff builds up. There is not one grain of yeast in the house. Meanwhile the brother has an evil eye toward another brother, or is bitter toward his wife, or vice versa. We sweep our houses with diligence; we must do the same with our spirit, because we are the temple of God.

“If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” You will pull this out on a brother in the street: brother, you got tattoos, you got the devil on you, you are defiling your temple. We know tattoos are wrong. But meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If you are out there with the leaven of bitterness in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if he and you do not repent.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” What is that really saying? How do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps into your mind and you say, damn, I don't like that brother. You are spiritually consuming it, entertaining sin and not purging the leaven from your house. That is how you get cut off from your people, and this is a serious thing.

How you get cut off: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Christ is our Passover, who set the example. That is the gift, the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins, because we are in a wicked place.

And Exodus 13:7 says “there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.” We do not want to be seen in the midst of sin, Passover or not. Don't be the brother who does not throw the bread out but puts it in his storage closet and brings it back when Passover is over: laying the bitterness aside for the season and picking right back up hating the brother. That is not the spirit. Throw it out. Let it go.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20
precepts.why:
Some brothers say, I am going to tuck mine in, tuck away my hatred and my bitterness and save it for later. Paul answers that: “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?”

We are not our own. So when we hide hatred, bitterness, malice, whatever sins we deal with, we are throwing that back in Christ's face. He is our Passover, our sacrifice; he bought us back, twice he bought us back. So we do not own our bodies to even have the angle to defile our temple. When a brother lends you something, you are supposed to take extra care of it. Christ gave us our bodies and bought us back again, and we need to keep them like brand new.

“For ye are bought with a price”: with Christ's blood. Then, “therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” We have to use our bodies to glorify him in every way possible, and our spirit too, because both belong to God. When we hold back malice, hatred for our brothers or hatred for our wife, we put that on Christ, and it is not of the Lord. We have to let go of that spirit.

That is the leaven Exodus 12:15 says to put out of your house: not only the yeast on the box, but the bitterness tucked in when Bishop comes around and let out again when he leaves.

precepts.label: Numbers 14:27-34
precepts.why:
Exodus 13:8 says “And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.” This is done means the feast of unleavened bread. But what did the Lord do unto me? The Lord delivered everyone, but did everyone enter the promised land? No. Numbers 14 shows what he did.

“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” When we came out of Egypt, our people were evil. You thought they were righteous? They were rebellious: a bunch of liars, fornicators, murmurers. The Lord said, “as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward”. Once you were twenty years old and up, the Lord said, all of you are going to die. Aaron died. Moses died too; not that Moses was evil, but the people provoked him to anger, so he did not see the promised land, though when he left his body he was going back to paradise.

“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.” Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to make it in. According to the law, at twenty you are the age of a man and take responsibility for yourself, which is why twenty is the age to marry. Everybody twenty and up, their blood was on their own head.

“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.” The children wandered forty years and bore the whoredoms of the adults, seeing all the evil they did, “until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness”: until every last one of those wicked Israelites died, everybody who had leaven in them, the murmurers, the adulterers, the ones who held on to Egypt.

So the me of Exodus 13:8 is not Moses. It is the little ones, twenty years and under, who grew up in the land and told their sons: we keep unleavened bread because the Lord purged the leaven out of me in the wilderness. And it is the same in the future: whoever keeps leaven, which is sin, through the seven days, that soul shall be cut off.

precepts.label: Proverbs 30:7-9
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.” To see what that means, go to Proverbs.

“Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.”

Lest I be full and deny thee: that is one way of taking his name in vain. Lest I be poor and steal: that is sin, and sinning while bearing his name is taking the name of my God in vain. We are called by his name; he says we are a holy people, and he put his spirit in us.

So when they say you cannot keep the commandments, why can’t we? That does not mean we have never sinned. All men have sinned, and if anybody says they have not sinned, they lie. But when they say you cannot keep the commandments, it is because they want to remain in their sins.

This sits inside the first four commandments, which go into loving the Lord thy God. All of this blending of religions is meant to take you away from serving him and to keep you in sin.

precepts.label: Leviticus 25:1
precepts.why:
Exodus 23 gives the seventh year release: work the land six years, “But the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat”. Leviticus 25 lays out the same law: “And the Lord spake unto Moses in mount Sinai, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the Lord”. He is telling us what to do when we enter the land, and we entered the land under Joshua, not under Moses.

“Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof; But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land”. Don't farm the land that year. “That which groweth of its own accord of thy harvest thou shalt not reap”: whatever grows on its own during the seventh year, that is what you eat. “And the sabbath of the land shall be meat for you; for thee, and for thy servant, and for thy maid, and for thy hired servant, and for thy stranger that sojourneth with thee”.

The seventh year release is built on the seventh-day Sabbath. Exodus 23 says it right after the land: “Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest”. The Sabbath goes for the land as well; when you have property, you let your land rest.

And the question everybody asks is answered in verse 20: “What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years”. The sixth year covers you for three years. Brothers and sisters say, I got to work on the Sabbath because that's my money day. Then you don't believe what we just read. That was the same question in verse 20, and God answered it: work six, rest on the seventh, and he provides.

precepts.label: Exodus 12:5
precepts.why:
Leviticus 23 lays out the feasts of the Lord, seven of them in that chapter, and every single one of them represents Jesus Christ. The first annual one is the Lord’s passover, “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even”, the high holy day we just celebrated. So we go back to the instructions for the passover lamb.

“Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats”. Without blemish, a male of the first year. That is the lamb our forefathers had to choose.

That lamb without blemish is the pattern of Christ. The passover is a representation of Christ laying down his life for us, and everything spoken of the lamb in Exodus 12 points to him.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 1:18-20
precepts.why:
Peter shows who that lamb without blemish was: “ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot”.

So Christ was that lamb without blemish, the same thing Exodus 12:5 required. Without blemish and without spot. He is the one “foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you”.

That is what John the Baptist said of Christ when he saw him coming: Behold the Lamb of God that takes away the sins of the world. The passover of Leviticus 23:5 is fulfilled in him.

precepts.label: Exodus 12:46
precepts.why:
Still in the passover instructions: “In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.”

Neither shall ye break a bone thereof. Those are the instructions for how to slaughter the lamb: do not break the bones of it.

That one command is going to be fulfilled to the letter in Christ. The high holy day of passover that we just went over is a picture of him, down to his bones.

precepts.label: Psalms 34:20
precepts.why:
Here is the prophecy about Christ: “He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.”

What was commanded for the passover lamb in Exodus 12:46, “neither shall ye break a bone thereof”, is written here as a prophecy of the Messiah. Not one of his bones would be broken.

The passover is a representation of Christ laying down his life for us, and the Psalms spoke it ahead of time, so that when it came to pass we would know he is our passover.

precepts.label: John 19:31-33
precepts.why:
This is the fulfilment. “The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken”.

“Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs”.

They broke the legs of the two crucified with him, but not his. Thus fulfilling the prophecy in Psalms 34:20, and the passover command, neither shall ye break a bone thereof. Christ was that passover lamb, and there is still more meat to scrape off the bones of this.

precepts.label: Micah 5:2
precepts.why:
The lambs without blemish were raised in Bethlehem and slaughtered in Jerusalem. Same thing as Jesus Christ. So the prophecy: “But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.”

Christ was born in Bethlehem. An article read in the class shows how our forefathers handled the passover lambs: the high priests given charge over them brought forth lambs without blemish from Migdal Eder in Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and brought them to Jerusalem for sacrifice. Migdal Eder means the tower of the flock, the same tower of the flock read about in Micah the fourth chapter, the eighth verse.

This Jesus was born in Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and eventually brought to Jerusalem during passover, where he offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins. The same road as the lambs.

precepts.label: Luke 2:4-7
precepts.why:
“And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.”

To be taxed together you have to be married, brothers. You have to have papers, jointly. Not a toilet paper: years ago a brother wrote an instrument of divorce on toilet paper, because he did not really value her or count her as his wife.

“And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes”. They wrapped Christ in swaddling clothes, the same thing our forefathers did with the lambs when they brought them to Jerusalem.

Born in Bethlehem where the passover lambs were raised, wrapped the way they were wrapped, offered in Jerusalem at passover. Thus fulfilling prophecy. So we know Christ was our passover.

precepts.label: John 6:35
precepts.why:
After passover comes the next feast: “on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.” There is that seven again.

The unleavened bread represents Christ: his sinless life, not having leaven. We know the history too, the Most High wanted us to hurry up and leave Egypt, so there was no time to sit and bake bread. But it also goes into Christ’s unleavened life, sinless and blameless.

Christ says it: “I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger”. He is the bread of life, the unleavened bread of the feast.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

The old leaven is sin. Purge it out, that you may be a new lump. Because Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.

Christ was that unleavened bread that laid his life down for the children of Israel. So the passover and the feast of unleavened bread in Leviticus 23:5-6 both come to him: he is the lamb and he is the bread. With these the class counted three of the seven so far: the Sabbath, the passover, and the feast of unleavened bread.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 15:20-23
precepts.why:
The two wave loaves of Leviticus 23:17 “are the firstfruits unto the Lord.” Paul shows who the firstfruits are: “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.” Christ is the firstfruits.

“For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.” Then the order is set: “But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.”

The same promise stands for us if we believe and keep the commandments in the faith of Christ: first Christ was raised, and afterward we that are his are raised at his coming.

Like the sabbath, the passover and the feast of unleavened bread before it, the feast of firstfruits is a representation of Christ. All seven of the high holy days read in Leviticus 23 represent Jesus Christ, and seven sabbaths counted “complete” to the fifty days points to completion in him.

precepts.label: Romans 8:23
precepts.why:
Christ is the firstfruits, and his people are called firstfruits with him: “And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.”

Redemption of what body? The body that we used to have, when we were in the heavens with Christ. That is what we groan and wait for.

We are supposed to be the firstfruits: the crème de la crème, the best of the best, if we would repent in Christ. So the “firstfruits unto the Lord” brought out of Israel’s habitations in Leviticus 23:17 point not only to Christ risen, but to the Israelites who have his Spirit and wait for their redemption.

precepts.label: James 1:18
precepts.why:
James says it the same way: “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.”

The Most High, of his own will, begat us with the word of truth for this purpose, that we should be a kind of firstfruits. We become that if we follow after Christ’s example, since Christ is the firstfruits risen from the dead.

So the feast of firstfruits in Leviticus 23:15-17, the new offering brought to the Lord after seven sabbaths complete, is a picture of Christ and of the people he begets by the word: the best of the best, offered unto the Lord.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:4
precepts.why:
Revelation shows the firstfruits standing with Christ: “These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins.” Not defiled with philosophy, not defiled with false doctrine, and also not defiled with a literal woman.

“These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.” They follow Christ wherever he goes, and they are redeemed from among men.

This is the end of the feast of firstfruits in Leviticus 23: Christ the firstfruits risen, and afterward those that are his, kept clean from the world’s doctrine and its filth, offered as “the firstfruits unto the Lord.”

precepts.label: Matthew 24:31
precepts.why:
Why do we blow the trumpet? Because it was commanded of us, on the new moons and on our high holy days: “a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.” But like every one of these feasts, it is a representation of Christ.

Christ says: “And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” The trumpet sounds at his coming, and it gathers his elect.

The elect is only Israel, not all nations. They are gathered “from one end of heaven to the other” because we were scattered from one end of heaven to the other. That tells you who the children of God are: the only people scattered from one end of the earth to the other are the so-called blacks and Hispanics, the Israelites.

So the feast of trumpets looks forward to that great sound, when Christ sends his angels to gather his scattered people home.

precepts.label: Zechariah 9:14-16
precepts.why:
That trumpet is not talking about a flute or some soft sound. When Christ comes back, everybody is going to fear. Zechariah shows it: “And the Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning: and the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south.” This is when we are going to conquer the nations.

“The Lord of hosts shall defend them; and they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones”. We are going to devour all these nations, put them under our feet, break them in half. Then “they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine; and they shall be filled like bowls, and as the corners of the altar.”

“And the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” The Most High said he is going to save us. That is some beautiful stuff right there.

So the memorial of blowing of trumpets in Leviticus 23:24 points to the day the Lord God himself blows the trumpet, defends Israel, and lifts his people up like the stones of a crown upon his land.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:23
precepts.why:
The trumpet sound at Christ’s coming is no flute and no harmonica. Ezra says: “And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid.”

That is how you know it is not talking about a soft sound or any instrument you could think of. Every man who hears it is suddenly afraid. That trumpet is a frightening sound.

It lines up with Matthew 24:31, the “great sound of a trumpet” that gathers the elect, and with Zechariah 9:14, where “the Lord God shall blow the trumpet” and his arrow goes forth as the lightning. The feast of trumpets in Leviticus 23:24-25 is a memorial pointing to that day: the gathering of Israel, and terror for the nations.

precepts.label: Hebrews 7:22-25
precepts.why:
The day of atonement, when Israel was to “afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord”, is a representation of Christ. Christ was that atonement.

“By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.” The better testament is the new covenant. “And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death”: the priests under the law died, one after another.

“But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him”. Christ is the true high priest, with no death in him. That is how he is able to atone for our sins continually, where the old priests could only atone until they died.

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:11-18
precepts.why:
“But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.” His blood was given for atonement, and he died only once. Eternal redemption for whom? For us, the Israelites.

“For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” Without spot means blameless: he had no sin.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament”, just as Moses was the mediator for us when we came up out of Egypt, so “that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” That promise is ours if we believe.

“For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.” For the testament to come to fruition and be valid, the testator had to die. That is why Christ had to die. “For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.” While a man is alive, his testament can still change. “Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.” Blood had to be spilled for the first covenant of animal sacrifice too. The yearly atonement of Leviticus 23:27 was fulfilled once for all in Christ’s own blood.

precepts.label: Romans 3:25
precepts.why:
Paul names what Christ is: “Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood”. God sent Christ forth, and propitiation means atonement.

He was set forth “to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God”. The sins that are past are forgiven through faith in his blood, by God’s forbearance toward us.

So the day of atonement, when Israel afflicted their souls and brought an offering by fire, finds its meaning in Christ. He is the atonement God himself set forth, and we receive it through faith in his blood.

precepts.label: 1 John 2:2
precepts.why:
John says it plainly: “And he is the propitiation for our sins”. Christ is the atonement for our sins, the fulfilment of the day of atonement in Leviticus 23:27.

Then: “and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.” That world is the scattered Israelites, all Israel, so that they may have time to repent. It is talking about Israel; it is not talking about all nations.

The next reading shows it: in the high priest’s long garment “was the whole world”, and that world was the twelve tribes. So when Christ atones for the world, he atones for Israel wherever they have been scattered.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:24
precepts.why:
Remember, Christ is the new high priest. Wisdom shows what the high priest carried: “For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and thy Majesty upon the diadem of his head.”

That is Aaron the high priest, and the long garment is the ephod. There was a stone for each tribe. The whole world on Aaron’s chest was Israel. It did not represent the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Hittites, the Perizzites or the Ishmaelites; only the Israelites.

That is how 1 John 2:2 is understood: Christ is “the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.” The world the high priest bore before God on the day of atonement was the twelve tribes, and the world Christ atones for as the new high priest is scattered Israel.

thread.label: Leviticus 23:34
thread.text: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: John 1:14
precepts.why:
“The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord.” Another word for tabernacles is sukkot, booths, and it means to dwell.

John shows who the feast points to: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,)”. The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us: he pitched his tent among us. Christ walked among us.

So the feast of tabernacles, like the sabbath, the passover, unleavened bread, firstfruits, trumpets and atonement before it, is a representation of Christ. The seven days of dwelling in booths look to the Son of God coming to dwell with his people in the flesh.

precepts.label: John 2:19-21
precepts.why:
“Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” The Jews took him simply: “Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?” They thought he meant the building.

“But he spake of the temple of his body.” His body is the temple, the tabernacle. Hebrews 9:11 shows it: “But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building”. His body was that greater and more perfect tabernacle. “Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.”

So the booths Israel dwelt in for the feast of tabernacles point to Christ’s own body, the true tabernacle in which God dwelt among us, destroyed and raised up again in three days.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:3
precepts.why:
“And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them”. That is what tabernacle means: to dwell. He shall dwell with whom? The Israelites.

Then: “and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.” All praises to the Most High for that. He is not the God of the Ishmaelites, not the God of the Arabs, not the God of the white man. He is the God of Israel only.

This is the completion every feast was pointing to. All seven of the high holy days read in Leviticus 23, and there are more, represent Jesus Christ, and the feast of tabernacles ends where the scriptures end: God dwelling with his people Israel for ever.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: Leviticus 25:23
precepts.why:
The whole Jubilee rests on this: “The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me.” Israel could sell the use of a field, but never the field itself, because the land belongs to the Most High. He is the owner, and he decides its proper use. That is why nobody in Israel was to heap up land for himself: it never really belonged to them.

That is also why the price of land was worked by the harvests left until the Jubilee. “According to the multitude of years thou shalt increase the price thereof, and according to the fewness of years thou shalt diminish the price of it: for according to the number of the years of the fruits doth he sell unto thee.” More years means more crops, so a higher price; one year left means one harvest, so the price has to be less. What was bought was the crops, not the land. And in the middle of it: “Ye shall not therefore oppress one another; but thou shalt fear thy God”.

Look at how black people chip each other and undercut each other today. That is why we have to come back to the Bible and apply these basic principles. When our own try to oppress one another in business, our people go to the Chinese man instead. God says don't oppress one another.

The Most High even provided for the year they could not farm. “What shall we eat the seventh year?” “Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years.” That answers everyone who says they have to break the Sabbath to make their money. It is connected to the seventh-day Sabbath, where what was needed was baked beforehand and laid up for the seventh; here it is the sixth year he increases. It is all spiritual.

Read on: “And in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land.” If a brother waxed poor and sold some of his possession, a kinsman could come and redeem what he had to sell away. If none could, and he later had the means himself, he counted the years and restored the overplus, the extra. And if he could not, the land stayed in the hand of the buyer only “until the year of jubile”, and then he returned to his possession, money or no money. Every fifty years it all goes back.

There is a spirit in the land. The woman who came to Esdras was Jerusalem, and the Most High wanted us to see that there is a connection between the people and the land. So when the trumpet sounds on the Day of Atonement in the fiftieth year and liberty is proclaimed, every man returns to his possession and his family, because the land was never anybody's to keep but the Lord's.

thread.label: Leviticus 25:39
thread.text: And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant:

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: Leviticus 25:44
precepts.why:
After the law for a poor brother comes the distinction: “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.” Your bondmen and bondmaids shall be of the heathen, the other nations. A bondservant is like chattel slavery, and that is what Israel was never to make of a brother.

Keep reading: “Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.” Now the word stranger is talking about the heathen, as the verse above explained. “And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? For ever. They got passed down from generation to generation, to your son and your daughter. The other nations were not released in the Jubilee; they remained slaves. That is what God said.

Then the stress on but: “but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.” There is the distinction. Your brother who waxes poor and is sold to you serves “as an hired servant, and as a sojourner”, what we call a job today; back then they called you a servant. He serves until the Jubilee, and then “shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family”. “For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.” “Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour; but shalt fear thy God.” Rigour is hardship: busting him in the head, whooping him. Don't do that.

The word stranger in this chapter does not always mean another race. The stranger of verse 35, “though he be a stranger, or a sojourner”, is a brother of another tribe, like Judah living in the land of Simeon, a stranger there. Numbers 16:40 shows it: “no stranger, which is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to offer incense before the Lord”. Anyone not of the seed of Aaron, Judah, Benjamin, Manasseh, Ephraim, Gad, Reuben, was called a stranger. But in verses 44 and 45 the stranger is the heathen round about.

So the Jubilee's liberty was for Israel. The poor brother went free; the bondmen of the heathen did not. “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt”. Verse 55 tells you plain: the Israelites are God's servants. Everybody on the planet is not God's servants.

precepts.label: Leviticus 25:48
precepts.why:
When a brother waxed poor and sold himself to a sojourner or stranger, it was not the end of him: “After that he is sold he may be redeemed again; one of his brethren may redeem him”. This is not saying we sold ourselves to the other nations. It is another tribe. A man of Judah whose land is jacked up goes among the tribe of Gad and says, I'm poor, I need to work for you, help me. Esau will use this chapter and try to cause confusion with that word stranger, saying see, the other nations. No. That is about Israel.

“Either his uncle, or his uncle’s son, may redeem him, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family may redeem him; or if he be able, he may redeem himself.” A kinsman could buy him back, and if he came into some money while he was working, he could say, I don't need this anymore, and redeem himself.

The price was reckoned the same way as the land: “from the year that he was sold to him unto the year of jubile: and the price of his sale shall be according unto the number of years, according to the time of an hired servant shall it be with him.” The price is according to the years left from now to the Jubilee. “If there be yet many years behind”, the price of his redemption is higher; “if there remain but few years unto the year of jubile”, it is lower. It is the same concept as the land.

“And as a yearly hired servant shall he be with him: and the other shall not rule with rigour over him in thy sight.” That goes back to verse 43. “And if he be not redeemed in these years, then he shall go out in the year of jubile, both he, and his children with him.” That goes back to verse 41.

Why? “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” A poor brother of Israel is never a bondservant for ever. He is the Lord's servant, he can always be redeemed, and in the Jubilee he goes free with his children.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
In the wilderness the children of Israel wept and said, “We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. What are they saying? Deuteronomy 28:48 explains it.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Serving our enemies in hunger and in thirst is one of the curses that was upon us, and it was also a curse that was on us in ancient Egypt. We had to serve the Egyptians for the want of all things. It is the same today: you need money to buy food, and you have to serve for it.

Back then we had fish, because the Nile was abundant in fish, and we had melons. So brothers got delivered from oppression and started talking about going back to Egypt: even though we were oppressed, at least there we had some good food. It is the same thing with us here in America. A lot of you have food, you are full, you are comfortable. Well, for now.

precepts.label: Leviticus 18:3
precepts.why:
It was not just that the Egyptians fed us. Everything we learned, we learned from the Egyptians back then. So when we came out of Egypt, God said: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do”.

Why did God say not to do after the doings of Egypt? Because we learned the Egyptian customs while we were there, the Egyptian names of the week. It is the same way here in America: you talk about Monday and Tuesday and all of that, days named after their gods, and all that is idolatry.

So God says, everything you learned in Egypt, forget it. The people who longed for the fish and the melons of Egypt were still holding on to Egypt in their hearts. And it is going to be the same thing when we are delivered up out of here, out of spiritual Egypt: everything we learned from this land, we will have to leave behind.

precepts.label: Exodus 14:11-12
precepts.why:
Numbers 14:22 says they “have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice”. These ten times are the countless acts of stubbornness of the children of Israel, and that is why the Lord asked “How long will this people provoke me?” Write them down. The Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

Number one is at the Red Sea. “And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt? Is not this the word that we did tell thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.”

They were complaining to Moses. The Lord had just brought them out with his glory and his miracles, and the first thing they did at the sea was wish themselves back in Egypt serving the Egyptians.

precepts.label: Exodus 15:23-24
precepts.why:
Number two of the ten times the children of Israel tempted the Lord is at Marah, m-a-r-a-h. Write it down so you are not confused if it comes up again.

“And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah. And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?”

The people complained because the water was bitter. They had just seen the Lord overthrow the Egyptians in the midst of the sea, and at the first bitter water they murmured against Moses. That is the provoking the Lord speaks of in Numbers 14:22: men “which have seen my glory, and my miracles”, and still did not hearken to his voice.

precepts.label: Exodus 16:2-3
precepts.why:
Number three is the wilderness of Sin. “And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness”. Do you notice a trend here?

“Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.”

It is going to be the same thing when Christ comes back, but Christ is not playing games with us this time; he did not play games back then either. This time it will be ten times worse, ten times more severe, ten times more strict. When we are saved out of this modern day Egypt, Babylon the Great, America, the United Snakes of America, and Christ brings us into the wilderness, that grace is finished. No more I should have, could have, would have, I made a mistake. That is over with.

precepts.label: Exodus 16:19-20
precepts.why:
Number four is the hoarding of the manna. “And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.” Moses gave specific instructions: do not leave any of the manna until the morning.

“Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.” Moses just told you. And they said, the hell with you; we want to replace you anyway. That is the mindset of our people.

This is what the Lord means in Numbers 14:22 when he says they “have not hearkened to my voice.” He fed them bread from heaven, gave one plain instruction, and they would not keep it.

precepts.label: Exodus 16:27-29
precepts.why:
Number five is the Sabbath manna. “And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none. And the Lord said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws? See, for that the Lord hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.”

They were supposed to gather extra on the sixth day; the Most High gave them enough manna to lay up for two days. And they said, no, Lord, we are going out on the seventh day to get this manna. Forgetting everything the Most High did for us in bringing us up out of Egypt. No gratitude. We are a people of no gratitude at all.

precepts.label: Exodus 17:2-7
precepts.why:
Number six is at Massah and Meribah. “Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink.” To chide means to murmur, to be contentious, to go back and forth. “And Moses said unto them, Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?”

Then, “the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.” They were almost ready to stone the man who brought them out of Egypt, over water.

The Lord said, “Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink.” And Moses “called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?”

That is the very word Numbers 14:22 uses: they have “tempted me now these ten times.” The place itself was named for it.

precepts.label: Exodus 32:1-10
precepts.why:
Number seven is the golden calf. “And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.”

That is the no gratitude. The Most High just showed all those wonderful plagues and destroyed your enemy, and now you want a different god, a god of silver, gold and wood, a god that cannot talk. And look how disrespectful: as for this Moses. No different from our people who despise this truth and want to go back to Christianity, who prefer white Jesus, or who run to the east, to Mecca, and pray to a damn cobblestone that cannot talk back or answer prayers. That is why the Most High says we are dumber than an ox.

Aaron, the high priest, got real simple here, but it was out of fear, and he knew better. Then, “he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf”; he had the skills of a blacksmith and turned the gold they spoiled from Egypt into idolatry. It was the people who said “These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” Then “the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play”: in honour of that pagan god they had orgies.

“They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them”. “I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people: Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them”. Yes, we are a stiffnecked people, and only Moses standing in the gap turned it away, as he did again in Numbers 14.

precepts.label: Numbers 11:1-6
precepts.why:
Number eight is Taberah. “And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord: and the Lord heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the Lord burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.” More complaining, and the Most High started burning people with fire, the same thing he is going to do in America. “And the people cried unto Moses; and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched.”

Then the lusting for flesh: “the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. Always about food; black people for you.

“But now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes.” Ungrateful, complaining about the manna. Over and over the Lord was longsuffering, and over and over Moses prayed and the Lord pardoned, as Numbers 14:20 says: “I have pardoned according to thy word”.

precepts.label: Numbers 11:34
precepts.why:
Number nine: the lusting for flesh ended in a graveyard. “And he called the name of that place Kibroth–hattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.” Taberah was number eight; Kibroth-hattaavah is number nine.

Number ten is the report of the spies, the doubt and fear of Numbers 13 and 14, and there the Most High had enough. “Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it”. Everyone twenty and upward fell in the wilderness, save Caleb and Joshua.

The Most High deals in numbers, and everything in the Bible is significant. Ten times he was longsuffering, and places like Kibroth-hattaavah still carry the names of what our fathers did.

precepts.label: Tobit 4:12
precepts.why:
Numbers 36 is the law for the brother who had no sons. The chief fathers of Gilead, of the tribe of Manasseh, came before Moses because the inheritance of Zelophehad was given to his daughters, and “if they be married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Israel, then shall their inheritance be taken from the inheritance of our fathers”. The inheritance goes to her husband. Not even the jubile would bring it back: “so shall their inheritance be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.” You are Manasseh, you marry into Judah, and Judah owns that land forever.

So the Lord commanded, “only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry”, “that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.” That is the law right there: if you have all daughters and you have land and property, they marry within the tribe so another tribe of Israel does not take possession of it forever.

That is what Tobit was making reference to. Brothers often ask, because Judah married outside the tribe of Judah and Ephraim married outside the tribe of Ephraim. But there was a special clause when it came to property and land, and the woman was not allowed to do that.

Tobit tells his son, “chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. See that: not of thy father’s tribe. “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”, and “our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.” Shall inherit the land: that is the point. Marrying your own kindred is how the inheritance of the fathers stays with their seed.

precepts.label: Tobit 4:13
precepts.why:
Tobit keeps going, and it is for anybody here looking at a Chinese lady: “love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them: for in pride is destruction and much trouble”. It is pride when you do not want to marry a woman of your own race, your own tribe. When people say love is love, that has nothing to do with it; God never said hate your people.

“and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.” You will lose everything, and you see it all in the news. Halle Berry married outside and now pays child support to both of her exes, thousands every month, while the white husband she paid called her a nigger every time she paid. He fought to straighten and lighten their daughter’s natural hair, because he wanted his children to look white. She knew what she was up against.

Serena and Venus Williams married outside the race after all the hell their father went through for those two girls. He saw the power of white supremacy get into his daughter’s head, and he did not show up at the wedding. Janet Jackson married an Arab and ran out of there with the baby, under an agreement not to speak on what she saw. Shannon Sharpe lost millions and millions of dollars over a twenty-year-old white girl from the gym.

That is lewdness being the mother of famine, decay and great want. The Bible is a true book. The law of Numbers 36 kept the inheritance in the tribe of the fathers, and Tobit shows the curse on those who despise their own people and take a strange woman.

classes.title: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.label: James 2:1
precepts.why:
Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

precepts.label: James 2:4
precepts.why:
“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

precepts.label: James 2:9
precepts.why:
“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend's folly; none of us should.

What has been discovered is that because someone is your friend, you do not want to speak out. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. Something is wrong with that. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.

precepts.label: Joshua 23:12
precepts.why:
“Else if ye do in any wise go back, and cleave unto the remnant of these nations, even these that remain among you, and shall make marriages with them, and go in unto them, and they to you”. We were forbidden to make marriages with the other nations. Deuteronomy 7 gives the reason: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.”

What happens if we do it? “Know for a certainty that the Lord your God will no more drive out any of these nations from before you; but they shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land”. The nations you marry become snares and traps to you.

Look at the examples. A black woman who no longer thought she looked good as a black woman now looks like the Joker. A black woman doctor, and the best she could get looks like Quasimodo, the Hunchback of Notre Dame. A Kenyan woman vanished after meeting a 400-pound white boyfriend on Craigslist. Many of these women said the white man is better than the black man, and they were put to death. Black men too: a brother on Twitter spoke much evil about black women, and a white woman stabbed him to death, and she is home celebrating Christmas. Sherrone Moore already had a white woman at home, but needed a young white woman, gave her a six-figure job, and lost about 21 million dollars of his contract; he lost everything for a white coontang. Shannon Sharpe lost his ESPN role over a white woman he met, settling for millions. Halle Berry pays 8,000 dollars a month to that Edomite, who called her a nigger: he takes the money and says, Thank you, nigger, and walks away. That is a snare and a trap. God said do not do it.

Tobit 4:12 says the same: “Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”, for our fathers “all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children”. Look at the biracial children, so many confused and bugged out; it is rare when they know exactly who they are.

We had these laws from the beginning. In Genesis 6, “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Before the flood we were called the sons of God. We went in unto the daughters of men, had children with them, and “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” That is Psalms 82: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” We accepted the persons of the other nations, so we die like men, and fall like the other nations, and God will not drive them out while we cleave to them.

thread.text: Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: Genesis 15:18
precepts.why:
Before Genesis, Deuteronomy 11 was read from verse 21, the word the Lord gave Israel in advance of entering the land: “That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” For us, heaven has always been upon the earth. If Israel would diligently keep the commandments, “Then will the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.” To possess means to own. Then: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours”. Every place your feet touch is your land; that is heaven on earth.

With a map on the screen, verse 24 lays out the borders. “From the wilderness” is the wilderness of Egypt, on the other side of the Nile. “And Lebanon” sits at the top of the map, and Lebanon was ours. “from the river, the river Euphrates” runs through Syria, just above Lebanon. “even unto the uttermost sea” is the Mediterranean on the left. So the land ran from the wilderness of Egypt all the way up to the Euphrates, taking in Syria and everything down from it.

Genesis 15:18 goes with Deuteronomy 11:21-24. “In the same day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates”. The river of Egypt is the Nile. The same land God promised Abraham is the land Israel took. We were fighting from the time of Joshua to get all of it, and we fully had it under David and Solomon.

This matters for Jubilee. Jubilee did not start until Israel got into the land: count seven times seven years, forty-nine, and the fiftieth year is the jubilee, when the land rests and every piece of land goes back to the original owner of that heritage, that tribe. So the land has borders, and they are in the Middle East. The doctrines going around that the Congo, or Kenya, is the real Israel cannot stand. What are y'all talking about? It gives you the land layout right here. The hell is this?

From there Isaiah 14 shows the land coming back: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. He is not having mercy on everybody, only Jacob. We may be at the bottom of society, but he will yet choose Israel, and it is God who sets us in the land, not the League of Nations or the United Nations. “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”: every nation goes back to the land God first gave it, and “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”. The laws of Leviticus 25 cannot be in effect now while we are the slaves in a foreign land, but when we return to the land they go back into full effect.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 31:10
precepts.why:
“At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles”. Moses ties the year of release to a set time: every seventh year, in the feast of tabernacles. In that solemnity the land was released, the servants were released, and the debt was released.

It comes right after the Sabbath of the land in Leviticus 25. When the people ask, “What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase”, God answers, “Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years.” Think about that with the seventh day Sabbath. Brothers and sisters say, I have to work on the Sabbath because that is my money day; that is the same question as verse 20, and it shows you do not believe what was read. Work six days and rest on the Sabbath, and the Most High will provide.

Deuteronomy 15:1 then goes into more detail on what that year of release in Deuteronomy 31:10 is: “At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release”, and every creditor that lends to his neighbour, his brother, shall release it, “because it is called the Lord’s release.” Lend something, and at the end of seven years that debt is taken care of.

precepts.label: Matthew 26:11
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 15:11 says, “For the poor shall never cease out of the land”, and Christ said the same: “For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.”

Notice what that tells us. In verses 5 and 6 the Lord promised that if we carefully hearken to observe all the commandments, “thou shalt lend unto many nations, but thou shalt not borrow; and thou shalt reign over many nations, but they shall not reign over thee.” That happened in the time of David and Solomon. There would even be no poor among us. But in verse 11 he says the poor shall never cease out of the land. The Lord was letting us know we were not going to be keeping those commandments too long.

So the command stands: “Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.” If there be a poor man of one of thy brethren, “thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother”, but lend him sufficient for his need. And beware of the wicked thought, “The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand”: imagine it is the sixth year, and you refuse your brother because in twelve months you will not get it back. If he cries unto the Lord against thee, “it be sin unto thee.” Give, and do not be grieved, and the Lord will bless you in all your works.

This is also why the Hebrew servant sold to you, a brother who was poor and lacked food, water and shelter, served only six years and was not sent away empty, but furnished liberally out of the flock, the floor and the winepress, so he or she could have a fresh start and be self-sufficient. It is because we were bondmen in Egypt and the Lord redeemed us. All the laws intertwine with love thy neighbour as thyself.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:60
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:15 says that if we will not hearken unto the voice of the Lord to do all his commandments and his statutes, “all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. Verse 27 names one of them: “The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt”. Then verse 60: “Moreover he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, which thou wast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee.”

That is what we need to see. The curses of Deuteronomy 28 did not just come out of nowhere. A lot of them are the same curses that were on us in ancient Egypt: the botch of Egypt, the diseases of Egypt, the oppression of Egypt. God said in Exodus 3:9, “I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.” Our forefathers were oppressed in ancient Egypt, and they were oppressed here in America, and are still being oppressed here. The oppression is real.

So when the scripture calls America spiritually Egypt, it is because the same things that happened to us in ancient Egypt happened to us here, and the curses show it. The diseases of Egypt cleave unto us in this land, along with the rest: we grope at noonday, we do not prosper in our ways, and as a nation of people we are only oppressed and spoiled evermore.

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”. Moses is being very specific, and Exodus 14:13 explains it. At the Red Sea he told the people: “Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.”

The scripture already said we would never see those Egyptians again, for ever. So when Moses says we will go into Egypt a second time, the Egypt he is speaking of cannot be ancient Egypt. The people would have said, Egypt again? We are going back to Egypt a second time? And he explains: I am not talking about the Egypt you just came out of. The way whereof I speak unto thee, thou shalt see it no more again. It is a different Egypt.

And this time we go into it with ships. Moses saw the end. The Lord showed him the Israelites thrown on cargo slave ships and brought here to America: the transatlantic slave trade. Egypt, from the Hebrew Mizraim, means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So going into Egypt again means going into captivity, misery and tribulation again, carried there on ships, sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen. That is why Revelation 11:8 calls the great city, Mystery Babylon, America, spiritually Egypt.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:22-24
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 29:22 speaks of “the generation to come of your children that shall rise up after you”. Who is that? Isaiah 66 shows it: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain.” The seed and the name that remain in the new heaven and new earth are the righteous of our people that make it, those of us that get the kingdom.

“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” After they come up to worship, “they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”. Go forth where? To look on this place, America. That is the same moment Deuteronomy 29 describes, when the generation to come and the stranger from a far land see the plagues of that land, “brimstone, and salt, and burning”, and ask, “Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land?”

After somebody dies, their carcase is supposed to just disappear. So this is letting you know it is something spiritual. “for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” They are in damnation, cast in hell, being tormented. That is why Deuteronomy 29 says the Lord will separate the man that did not repent unto evil.

There is a place of torment, and it will be set up when Christ returns. After this place is destroyed physically, a spiritual prison and damnation will be set up here, the place of torment for the devils that said, have you come to torment us before our time. Christ has the power over hell and death: he can give you life and immortality, or wake you up and torment you.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:2
precepts.why:
Christ has the power over life and death, which is why Daniel 12 says some shall awake. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Many of them are going to awake. Some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. When you die, you go to sleep, yes. But Christ has the power to wake your behind up and torment you.

That is what stands behind the carcases of Isaiah 66:24, whose worm does not die and whose fire is not quenched, and behind the land of Deuteronomy 29 that is all brimstone, salt and burning. Those who forsook the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers and served other gods do not simply die and disappear: they are awakened to shame and everlasting contempt. As 2 Esdras 9 says, read in the same moment, those who despised his law while the place of repentance was open “must know it after death by pain.” And the righteous awake to everlasting life, the seed and the name that remain.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 4:26-27
precepts.why:
In Deuteronomy 31 Moses says, “For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves”, and “evil will befall you in the latter days”. How is Moses able to say I know? Deuteronomy 4 shows what he saw.

“I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.” When we went into the land of Israel, our days were not going to be prolonged in it; we were going to be destroyed from off that land. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” Moses saw the Israelites being scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

He could see it because God showed it to him. In 2 Esdras 14, read right after, the Lord says, “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt”, and he held him on the mount a long season, the forty days and forty nights, and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Moses saw the secrets of the beginning, which is how he wrote Genesis, and he saw the end.

So Moses saw what would happen to us in the time of the Babylonians, the Greeks and the Romans, and he saw us here in America, in the transatlantic slave trade, and America being destroyed. That is why he could say with certainty that evil would befall us in the latter days: he had already seen it.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:15
precepts.why:
At Jericho it was sevens all the way through: “seven priests shall bear before the ark seven trumpets of rams’ horns: and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow with the trumpets.” Six days they went round once, and on the seventh day, the Sabbath day, seven times. “And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city.” Because of their faith, on the seventh day the Most High brought the walls down flat.

Revelation shows the same pattern at the end: “And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.” The seventh angel sounded the trump, and that brought forth completion. It is the same thing that happened when our forefathers walked around the walls of Jericho.

Seven represents completion and totality, and it also represents complete deliverance. Nothing is accidental with the Most High; he uses seven as a form of deliverance. From the beginning it has been there: the seventh day rest, Naaman dipped seven times, and Jericho compassed seven times by seven priests with seven trumpets.

So the seventh trumpet at Jericho gave Israel the city, and the seventh trumpet in Revelation gives the kingdoms of this world to our Lord and his Christ. All of this is a representation of Christ, and it points to the complete deliverance of Israel when he reigns.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 16:13
precepts.why:
David was anointed more than once, and it starts here in Bethlehem: “Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward.” Samuel anointed him in the midst of his brethren, and the Spirit of the Lord stayed on him from that day.

After Saul was dead, David went up to the cities of Hebron, and the men of Judah came and anointed David king over the house of Judah. So he was anointed again in Hebron, but only over Judah; he was the king of Judah in Hebron.

Then all the tribes came: “Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.” They remembered that “when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel”, and that the Lord had said, “Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.” So “they anointed David king over Israel.” Now he is king over all twelve. “In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah”: both kingdoms. And “David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.” Zion is the city of David.

But the beef was already there before the split. In 2 Samuel 19 the men of Israel asked, “Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away”; Judah answered, “Because the king is near of kin to us”: he is our tribe. Israel said, “We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye”: there are more of us than you, why can't we anoint him over here? “And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.” Judah cursed Ephraim out, and that enmity between the two stayed.

Ephraim felt more entitled, and in a way rightfully so: Joseph saved Israel from starvation in Egypt, Joshua of Ephraim brought us into the land and gave out the allotments, and Ephraim held Shiloh, Bethel and the first places of worship. So the anointing that began in the midst of David's brethren is also where the dividing hatred between Judah and Ephraim shows itself, a rivalry that went on long after David.

precepts.label: Tobit 4:12-13
precepts.why:
“But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh”. When you turn against the Lord in this, you turn against your neighbor too, because you are taking foreign women. We know it will turn your heart away from following the Lord, but what does it do to your brother? It says you hate your brother. Tobit shows it.

“Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. He calls interracial marriage whoredom. “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

“Now therefore, my son, love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them”. Don’t despise your brethren. Passing over the daughters of your own people for strange women is despising your brethren in your heart. “for in pride is destruction and much trouble, and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.”

That is exactly where Solomon went. The Lord had said of those nations, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and Solomon clave unto them in love. His wives turned away his heart after Ashtoreth, Milcom, Chemosh and Molech, and he built high places for them and for all his strange wives. That is how syncretism enters: through the strange wife, and it begins by despising your own people.
