precepts.label: Sirach 47:23
precepts.why:
Solomon fell in love with heathen women, the very nations of which the Lord said “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and they did. He built a high place for Chemosh for his Moabite wife and for Molech for his Ammonite wife, and did the same for all his strange wives. So the Lord was angry with Solomon, and the prophet Ahijah “rent it in twelve pieces” and told Jeroboam, “Take thee ten pieces”: the kingdom would be rent out of the hand of Solomon’s son, with one tribe left for David’s sake.

Sirach sums up what Solomon left behind him when he died: “Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him Roboam, even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel.” Rehoboam was an idiot. He did not listen to the elders; he listened to the friends he grew up with, and by his counsel he turned the people away.

“There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin”. Jeroboam, the mighty man of valor Solomon made ruler over the house of Joseph, plotted against Solomon to rush the prophecy, fled to Egypt, and came back to take the ten tribes. And he showed Ephraim the way of sin.

So the heart Solomon gave to his strange wives bore its fruit in the next generation: a foolish son on the throne of Judah, a king who led Ephraim into sin, and the kingdom divided in two. That is where the dividing hatred between the houses begins.

thread.text: And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:16-20
precepts.why:
Naaman was told, “Wash, and be clean”, and when he believed and obeyed the word of the prophet, he was clean. Isaiah shows what the true washing is: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil; Learn to do well”.

Put away the evil of your doings: that's the true washing. Cease to do evil, learn to do well. Action, action, action. Not speak well, do well. “seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.”

“though your sins be as scarlet”, bloodshot red, “they shall be as white as snow”, if you learn to do well. “though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.” But it hangs on obedience: “If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword”.

That is Naaman. At first he refused and went away in a rage. When he humbled himself and did according to the saying of the man of God, his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. His belief and his obedience are what made him clean.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:6-7
precepts.why:
Naaman believed that the word of the prophet would heal him if he followed the commandment, going down to the river Jordan and dipping seven times. That belief is what healed him of his leprosy.

David prays the same way: “Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.” Truth in the inward parts is what the Most High desires. Then: “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.”

The water of the Jordan did not do it by itself; the Jordan was muddy water, and Naaman would rather have had the rivers of Damascus. The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins. Naaman obeyed the word, and he was made clean, his flesh like the flesh of a little child.

precepts.label: Luke 3:3-4
precepts.why:
We read about Naaman going down into the river Jordan to be cleansed. Luke brings us back to that same river: John “came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins; As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”

The baptism of repentance, for the remission of sins, preached about Jordan. Naaman was washed of his leprosy in the Jordan, and John preached the washing away of sins in the same Jordan. Nothing is accidental with the Most High.

It was Christ who healed Naaman, working through Elisha by his spirit. And John in the Jordan was preparing the way of that same Lord.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:13
precepts.why:
“Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.” Christ went unto John the Baptist to be baptized, and in what river? Jordan: the same river that Naaman had to dip in seven times.

Seven represents completion. Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan, completion in the river Jordan, and his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. The number and the river both point to the same Christ.

Who did the healing for Naaman? Not Elisha on his own. Elisha was working by the spirit of Christ; Christ is the one who did the healing, and he used Elisha as the prophet. So when Christ himself comes to the Jordan, it is the same one who cleansed Naaman there, the one who makes us clean.

precepts.label: Luke 4:25-27
precepts.why:
Christ himself reached back and referenced this exact history. “I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land; But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.”

Then the point: “And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.” Of all the lepers, the one cleansed was the one who humbled himself, believed, and went down and dipped seven times according to the saying of the man of God.

And seven also represents complete deliverance. Naaman dipped seven times and was delivered from his leprosy; Christ, the one whose spirit healed him through Elisha, spoke of it himself.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 17:1
precepts.why:
“In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years”. Ahaz, wicked and weak, was over Judah, and Hoshea was over Ephraim, the northern kingdom. Hoshea “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him”.

“Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria”. This is Pul’s son. In 1 Chronicles 5 it was Pul, Tiglath-pileser, who came first and took Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh; now his son Shalmaneser comes and does the most. The northern kingdom was not taken all at once. It was done in waves: one group taken out here, some of Reuben, some of Asher there, until almost all of Ephraim was out of the land.

Hoshea became his servant and paid him, then conspired against him: “he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria”. He tried to align himself with Egypt to defy Assyria, so the king of Assyria bound him in prison, “went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years”, and “carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes”. That is modern day Iran, bordering Russia. From there our people kept migrating further and further east: the northern kingdom became Scythians, moving from Iran into Russia, some as far as China, some as far as Japan, where they became samurai.

Why it happened: “the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God”, and they “did secretly those things that were not right”. They thought God wasn’t watching; he saw it all. They built high places in every city, “rejected his statutes, and his covenant”, “followed vanity, and became vain, and went after the heathen”. So “the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only”. Yet “Judah kept not the commandments” either, and “the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel”. God was done with all twelve: the northern kingdom into captivity, and Judah next.

Then the land was filled with heathen: “the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel”. The Lord sent lions to kill them for their evil, so a priest was brought back to teach them “the manner of the God of the land”, how to sacrifice so they could stay in the land in Ephraim’s absence. “Howbeit every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made”. The northern kingdom was called Samaritans because Samaria was their capital, and these heathen sacrificed in the very high places Ephraim made for their idols. And “the men of Babylon made Succoth–benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima”.

So the carrying away in 1 Chronicles 5:26 was the start of this: God himself stirred up the kings of Assyria against the tribes that went whoring after other gods, and the northern kingdom was broken and scattered, with strangers set in their place.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 35:1
precepts.why:
Solomon offered “according to the commandment of Moses”, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the solemn feasts, “three times in the year”: the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks and the feast of tabernacles. It is the same law given in Deuteronomy 16:16: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God”, and “they shall not appear before the Lord empty.” So we are supposed to gather and give an offering three times a year. We come together.

But do we give a physical offering today? No. So what do we offer? We offer ourselves; we offer obedience. Sirach puts it plainly: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.”

Keeping the law is the offering. The one who takes heed to the commandment is not coming before the Lord empty; his obedience is his peace offering. That is how Israel keeps these feasts now, the feast of weeks, which is Pentecost, among them: by gathering together and bringing a life that keeps the commandments.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 19:5
precepts.why:
“Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.” That is the northern kingdom: they stopped going to Jerusalem to worship, and Jeroboam set up idols for them. So when Asa gathered “all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon”, the northern tribes are called strangers. And “they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” Whenever Judah was on point, Ephraim would follow along.

The next king shows the same thing. Jehoshaphat, a good king of Judah, reigned from 870 to 848 BC. “And Jehoshaphat dwelt at Jerusalem: and he went out again through the people from Beer–sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the Lord God of their fathers.” Who dwelt at Beersheba? Simeon: that was Simeon’s allotment of land. From Simeon’s land all the way to mount Ephraim, Jehoshaphat caused some of Ephraim to return back to the Lord.

“And he set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city, And said to the judges, Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment.” “Wherefore now let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.” Jehoshaphat was a righteous king, and he set the law back in place.

So Israel was without God, without a teaching priest and without law, and the Lord would always use Judah to bring Ephraim back in, every single time. When Judah was on point, Ephraim followed along; when Judah went off, Ephraim went even worse off.

precepts.label: Psalms 148:14
precepts.why:
Christ said he would send his angels to gather the elect from the four winds, and Isaiah names the elect: “Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect.” The Israelites would not be in one land; they would be scattered worldwide. Before the angels come for them, the Lord says, “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” So who are the saints?

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The children of Israel are the saints.

Now read Psalms 50 again with that. “He shall call to the heavens from above”: that is the angels he is calling to. “and to the earth”: the earth is you and I. And the message to both is the same, “Gather my saints together unto me.” That is what we read in Matthew 24, where Christ tells his angels to gather the elect, and it is the commandment to the prophets on earth too.

“those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice”: only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. So we are not supposed to be looking for other races and other nationalities. The work of gathering is for the twelve tribes of Israel, the saints, scattered to the four corners of the earth.

thread.text: God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:26
precepts.why:
“God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” See that little g: that is us. Asaph, with the Holy Spirit on him, records what we did wrong as the gods of the earth: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” So we walk on in gross darkness, and “all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” Everything is wrong. What is out of course because of our sins? Go to Genesis: “And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night.”

Now Isaiah shows the kingdom: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days.” Does the sun have phases of transition? No. So in the kingdom the moon, which is a sign of the world, will not go back into darkness again. It is going to stay right. And the sun we say is so bright is not bright at all next to what it will be: sevenfold.

It is “in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” Binding up the breach means gathering the twelve tribes of Israel back again. Acts 15 quotes the prophets: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down.” And Amos says, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof.” Right now it is still fallen; we are trying to gather ourselves together. He will build us as in the days of old, that we may possess, own, the remnant of Edom and all the heathen.

The moon's phases started when Adam fell: the quarters, then the black moon, then it comes back. Before the fall it did not phase. That is why Israel is told, “Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day”: when that brightness returns, we celebrate the Most High, because this is how it was in the beginning. When the Lord binds up the breach, the lights will be set back in course, and the moon will shine as the sun.

thread.label: Psalms 82:5
thread.text: They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” What do we not know? “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” God judges in the congregation of the gods, and we are those beings that were with Adam in the beginning, ruling and judging this earth. That is the branches and the boughs. “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes”: it was not like that in the beginning. That is what happened after Adam fell.

Paul shows what we are waiting for: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” We have an eternal body in the heavens, the same body we had with Adam in the beginning. After Adam sinned, the Lord appointed that all of us must come on the earth through Adam in the flesh and fight to get the kingdom, the same way Christ came and overcame.

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All the creatures are waiting for the sons of God to be manifest. In Genesis we are called the sons of God; we are called the twelve tribes of Israel. “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” We want to be delivered from this corrupted body.

Paul says of us, “even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” We want back the body we had in the beginning, before Adam fell. To some this is foolishness; to others it is the power of God. You have to see what the Bible says. That is faith.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:9
precepts.why:
The children of the most High “walk on in darkness” and “die like men.” Ezra cries out over it: “it had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam: or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.” Adam ruled the heaven and the earth. Now we live in heaviness, the nations whooping our behind, and after death look for punishment. “O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.” Adam was not the only one kicked out of paradise. All his children fell with him.

That is why Christ came and died for our sins. Through one man sin came into the world, so through one man life came. He walked perfect and died for our sins, and he will choose which of us go back with him to paradise to rule the heaven and the earth: the ones who are real, who ask forgiveness, who keep fighting and never give up.

Paul's wording shows where we came from: “Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?” Christ ascended, but first he descended. His being born on the earth is called descending. The lower parts of the earth are here in captivity, the nether parts of the earth where his sons were cast out, and they descended the same way, by being born into the earth.

Even the fathers' names show it. Jared means descend, or descent: the sons of God came down to the nether parts of the earth and died, as Adam died. And Enoch, dedicated, trained, came down, trained himself to conquer the flesh, walked perfect, “and he was not; for God took him”: he went back up to paradise.

precepts.label: Galatians 4:26
precepts.why:
“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” We do not understand the power we have, or where we came from. Paul tells us: “But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.”

A lot of times we read that and it goes over our heads, but pay attention to the wording. Jerusalem which is above is the mother of us all, meaning we all came from there. That is where we came from. There are different levels of understanding to these scriptures.

So when Christ says he is not of this world, and tells us we are not of this world and to love not the world, understand what he is saying. When the Bible says we are pilgrims and strangers on this earth, understand what it is saying. And when it says that if we had been mindful of whence we came, we might have had opportunity to return, understand what it is saying.

We are the sons of God cast down to the nether parts of the earth, walking in darkness and dying like men, but our mother is the Jerusalem above. You have to believe these things and understand them, because that is who you are.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Proverbs 8:22-23
precepts.why:
“Wisdom hath builded her house”. Who is this wisdom? Go back a chapter, where wisdom speaks: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.”

This is going into Christ and wisdom, one and the same, interchangeable. Christ is the ultimate wisdom, the complete wisdom, set up from everlasting before the earth was.

That is why chapter 9 says wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Seven represents completion, and Christ is complete wisdom. The house wisdom built stands on him, the one the Lord possessed in the beginning of his way.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:1-2
precepts.why:
Wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Let's see who this wisdom pertains to and who had these seven pillars. Isaiah: “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”. That is talking about Christ.

Now count what rests upon him. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”: that's one. “the spirit of wisdom”: two. “and understanding”: three. “the spirit of counsel”: four. “And might”: five. “the spirit of knowledge”: six. “and of the fear of the Lord”: seven.

Those are the seven pillars of wisdom that Christ had. Seven represents completion, so they represent complete spiritual perfection, and that is what Christ operated in. Wisdom's house on seven pillars is Christ, full of the spirit of the Lord in every part.

precepts.label: 1 John 1:9
precepts.why:
“He that covereth his sins shall not prosper”: when you try to cover that bitterness, the roots keep growing, and you are just bringing in dump trucks to load more soil on top of it. But whoso confesses shall have mercy, and John shows why: “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins”. The Lord is faithful and just when we confess our sins.

That goes all the way back to Leviticus. When you brought your sacrifice before the priest, that was a public confession. You had to walk through the midst of all Israel with your offering.

Now we have the white man, his walls and his technology. We have VPNs: yeah, don't nobody know I'm on OnlyFans, I got a VPN, I'm broadcasting from the Philippines. No, brother, the Lord sees right through it.

So in order to get over the root of bitterness we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. Covering it will never prosper; confessing it is how we get the mercy we all want.

precepts.label: James 5:16
precepts.why:
Confessing is not only to the Lord. James says: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 says, no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess your fault, and a brother might say, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit. Woo, man, I feel a lot better. All of this is common. We all have levels of bitterness; some have a higher degree than others, but everybody deals with a level of bitterness, a level of lust, a level of lack of faith.

That doesn't mean getting on the public announcement. It means you see a godly man and say, hey Cap, hey D, I have this going on, I need help with it. They are going to help you. They are not going to say, brother, you got the devil on you, get away from me. It is Satan telling us otherwise.

That is whoso confesseth and forsaketh: confessing to the Lord, confessing one to another, and being healed, instead of covering the sin and letting the root grow.

thread.text: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Matthew 11:28
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls us “a people laden with iniquity.” Christ answers that very word: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” Heavy laden with what? With sin, the iniquity Isaiah just named.

That is why we are in need of a saviour. We read the history of our forefathers in the wilderness: the Most High showed great signs and wonders, and we were still a stiff-necked, hard-headed people. We are “a sinful nation”, “a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters.” We forsake the Lord every time we sin, and we have “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger.” That is why the so-called blacks and Hispanics went into captivity, just as Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 laid out the curses for breaking the commandments. Many of our brothers and sisters are still going backward, moonwalking away from the Most High. Brothers and sisters, we cannot do it without Christ.

So be honest and sincere, even in prayer. Do not go to the Most High acting righteous when you are full of dead bones, sin and guile. None of us is righteous; we are trying, but there is sin still in us. Open your mouth and confess the things you are battling with.

“and I will give you rest.” That rest is not a good night’s sleep. It is our land, the kingdom of God, rulership for a thousand years under Christ. That is the true rest he is talking about, but we have to come unto him. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:14
precepts.why:
In the days of Ahaz, Ephraim conspired with the Syrians to overthrow Judah: the Syro-Ephraimite war. Rezin was the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah was king of Ephraim, and their plan was to take Judah's land and set the son of Tabeal as king over it. Ahaz was weak and wicked, and his heart shook “as the trees of the wood are moved”. But the Lord said the counsel of Syria and Ephraim would not stand: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

In Isaiah 8 the Lord brings “the king of Assyria, and all his glory” like a river over his banks. Assyria would rise up and conquer Ephraim, and also pass through Judah and take some portions of it, but not fully like Ephraim. “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought” … “for God is with us.” Isaiah's sons were born as signs that Ephraim and Syria would be overthrown by Assyria and would not succeed against Judah.

So the Lord tells Isaiah not to fear their confederacy, and not to be like Ahaz, cowardly and weak: “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread. And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel.” It says both. The Lord speaks of one Israel as two houses: the house of Judah and the house of Ephraim, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. And that stone of stumbling is Christ.

He is “for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem”, a trap to both houses, but specifically to those in Jerusalem. “And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.” The context has not changed. Not only did Ephraim fall physically and spiritually; Judah fell physically and spiritually too, but worse, because they stumbled at that stone.

Hosea shows Ephraim's side. His daughter Lo-ruhamah, no mercy: “I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away”, which is Assyria overthrowing Ephraim so that it be not a people. His son Lo-ammi: “for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” When you are not God's people and he is not your God, that makes you a Gentile, a heathen, a stranger, a non-Israelite. Judah read that and said, good, the hell with Ephraim, they are Gentiles, we don't deal with them anymore.

The rock ties it together. Moses said “He is the Rock, his work is perfect” … “a God of truth and without iniquity”, and “is not he thy father that hath bought thee?” That rock of Isaiah 8 is Christ, our God and our father, and the stone both houses of Israel stumbled over.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 34:9
precepts.why:
Under Josiah, when the money for the house of God was brought to Hilkiah the high priest, it was “the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites that kept the doors had gathered of the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of all the remnant of Israel, and of all Judah and Benjamin”.

Manasseh donated toward the temple in Jerusalem, and Ephraim donated too. Why “the remnant of Israel”? Because Assyria had taken most of them out of the land in waves; remnants remained, some idolatrous and some faithful. And that was during Josiah’s reign: whenever Judah is on point, Ephraim follows along.

Then Isaiah speaks to those same northern lands: “the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali”, afflicted “by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” Zebulun came to keep the Passover in Hezekiah’s day, and Tobit was of Naphtali. Galilee of the Gentiles is where the northern kingdom resided, and they were called Gentiles. “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light”: the people of verse 1, the northern kingdom.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, not all. He is the Prince of Peace because he must bring peace between those who have hatred for each other, so that there is no more division between the two kingdoms. “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”. The same Ephraim and Manasseh whose remnant gave to the house of God in Judah’s good days would see the light of the son born of Judah.

thread.label: Isaiah 14:1
thread.text: For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1
precepts.why:
“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Before he sets us in our land, he tells the twelve tribes what to do: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” We are the nation not desired, and God is instructing the twelve tribes to gather themselves together, to wake up.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.” That decree is the destruction that is prophesied to come. Get yourselves together before destruction comes. Things are moving at a quicker pace, and that is why the Bishop says he loves President Trump: he is forcing prophecies to come to pass and forcing the Israelites to do what the Bible says.

Who gathers? “Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” The meek are humble to God’s word, men and women who do his commandments without making excuses. We cannot gather with camps that say we are not keeping any Sabbath, or that throw you out for wearing fringes with a border of blue.

Then the judgment on the land: “For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation.” “I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant.” The Palestinians are not just pushed out; according to the Bible they are destroyed. “And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah”, “for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.” That is Israel set in their own land.

precepts.label: Amos 3:3
precepts.why:
“Gather yourselves together” does not mean gather with everybody. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?”

You get some morons that say, Let’s join ourselves with the camp that believes John the Baptist was a wicked nigger. You cannot join with that. Let’s join with the camp that believes men do not have to work: get seven women, eight women, and let them work for you. No, we cannot join with that.

Some people are simple, and they ask, Why aren’t y’all all together? This is why. Two cannot walk together unless they are agreed, and the ones who gather are those who “have wrought his judgment”, the meek who do God’s laws, seek righteousness and seek meekness.

So when the Lord will yet choose Israel and set them in their own land, the gathering before the decree is not one of mixed doctrines. It is a gathering of those agreed on God’s commandments.

precepts.label: Amos 9:11
precepts.why:
The Lord “will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Judah shall live on the sea coast, and it gets better: “For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.” And Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” The tabernacle of David is the twelve tribes, built again as in the days of old.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name.” There are people calling themselves Jewish today, and Jew comes from Judah, praise of Yahawah; they are not the praise of Yahawah. And people calling themselves Christians, the anointed ones; they are not the anointed ones.

“And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them.” There are waste cities all over there, and after Armageddon there will be more. And we will have servants: that is the strangers joined to the house of Jacob, the heathen round about us as bondmen and bondmaids, when that law goes back in full effect.

“And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God.” That is Isaiah 14:1 fulfilled: set in their own land, never pulled out again.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:27
precepts.why:
The first sign of a bitter brother is that he is easily offended; he will “make a man an offender for a word”. The next sign is that he holds grudges, the thing Leviticus 19:18 forbids: “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people”. And he is always revisiting past wrongs.

Proverbs names him: “An ungodly man diggeth up evil”. That is the bitter brother digging up evil, the plumber brother, digging up old ish. As we say up in the States, he's digging it up like he's a plumber.

“and in his lips there is as a burning fire.” That is deceit, and he is always hating. That is the brother with the banana on his lips, the certified hater like Cain: I don't like that. That's you.

So the one who makes a man an offender for a word is the same one who keeps digging up the old things. He lacks forgiveness, as Sirach 28 showed, and he will not let the past rest. Brother, you are not in the right spirit.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 20:22
precepts.why:
Another sign of bitterness is quiet resentment: they sit back and stew in silence. Sirach shows that brother: “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness”. He is the bitter bashful brother, brother BB.

“and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.” He'll say, man, brother, everything good. Then he is told, brother, I need you to go do this, this and this, and he says, yes sir. The whole time he is thinking, I ain't feel like doing ish for that MF. He says yes sir to your face, and he has no intention in his heart of doing it.

That is the same bitter spirit as the one that makes a man an offender for a word, only hidden. The loud one digs up evil; the bashful one smiles and resents in silence. Either way he destroys his own soul, and he overthrows himself.

thread.label: Isaiah 35:1-10
thread.text: The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.

precepts.label: Revelation 5:12-13
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the wilderness and the desert shall be glad and “blossom as the rose.” When we are delivered, the desert places in our land will blossom and trees will start springing up, because we are connected to the earth. When the righteous people start ruling, everything changes. The animals are free, and the creatures understand us. That may sound like church talk, but the donkey did talk to Balaam: why are you beating me? Revelation shows how far that understanding goes.

“Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.” Christ receives all these things.

“And every creature which is in heaven”: those are the angels. There are creatures in heaven. “and on the earth”: the animals created on the earth. “and under the earth”: creatures created in the earth, worms and such, and creatures living deep in the earth that nobody has ever seen. “and such as are in the sea”: leviathan, and creatures in the sea no human being has ever seen, that the Lord created. “and all that are in them”: everything that was created.

“heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever.” They heard what John said, and they understood it, all the creatures.

That is why the land itself rejoices in Isaiah 35. The whole creation answers to the Lord, and when “the glory of Lebanon” is given and they “see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of our God”, it is because the Lord will be on the earth, and everything will change.

thread.label: Isaiah 37:37
thread.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.

classes.title: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.label: Tobit 1:1
precepts.why:
Sennacherib came against Hezekiah and mocked his God, and one angel of the Lord went forth and smote “in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.” One angel killed 185,000 soldiers in their sleep. Judah was saved without bow or sword, just as Hosea said. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh”, and his own sons smote him with the sword while he worshipped in the house of Nisroch his god. He went home pissed off, and Tobit shows what he did.

Tobit was “of the tribe of Nephthali”, led captive in the time of Enemessar, which is the Greek form of Shalmaneser the fifth, out of “Nephthali in Galilee above Aser.” He is northern kingdom, carried to Nineveh. “I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the ways of truth and justice, and I did many almsdeeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineve, into the land of the Assyrians.”

“The most High gave me grace and favour before Enemessar, so that I was his purveyor”, overseeing the food and rations. When Enemessar died, Sennacherib his son reigned, the same Sennacherib that attacked Hezekiah and lost 185,000 men. Tobit “gave my bread to the hungry, and my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him.” Assyria was very brutal and vicious; they would take Israelites to the top of the walls and throw them off, and Tobit would bury his brothers broken in pieces on the ground.

“And if the king Sennacherib had slain any, when he was come, and fled from Judea, I buried them privily; for in his wrath he killed many.” Why did he flee from Judea? Because he lost 185,000 men. He was mad that he could not overthrow Judah, so out of anger he started killing Ephraim. When a Ninevite complained of Tobit to the king, his goods were forcibly taken away, and “there passed not five and fifty days, before two of his sons killed him”, the same death Isaiah 37:38 records.

Then Sarchedonus, Esarhaddon, reigned and appointed Achiacharus, Tobit's brother's son, over all his father's accounts, so Tobit gained standing again through his nephew. So Isaiah shows the angel saving Judah, and Tobit shows the other side of that same day: the northern kingdom in captivity in Nineveh, bearing Sennacherib's wrath, and a faithful Naphtalite burying his brethren.

thread.label: Isaiah 43:1
thread.text: But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:58
precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” And to redeem us, “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee. Since thou wast precious in my sight.” We are precious in his sight because we are the apple of his eye.

Ezra shows what we are to him: “But we thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn, thy only begotten, and thy fervent lover, are given into their hands.” We are his fervent lover. We are his bride. We are his wife.

That is why God gave Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba, which is Somalia, for our ransom: to deliver us out of captivity he had to destroy the Egyptian army, and Ethiopia that was a help to them. “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” In order for us to be delivered from slavery and captivity, God said, I have to destroy nations for them to release you.

So when Isaiah says “thou art mine”, it is the voice of a husband over his wife. The firstborn, the only begotten, the fervent lover given into the hands of the nations is the one God redeems.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:8
precepts.why:
“I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” Do you think the nations are just going to give his people back? No. Christ comes with armies: “And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” Wherever the Israelites are, the armies of God will go there and deliver us and destroy those nations.

The Christian mentality wants a white Jesus to come back throwing flowers, and John Hagee says Christ will set his government up to get the Democrats and Republicans in order. Wisdom of Solomon shows what salvation really is: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” We all want the salvation of the righteous, and we have to accept the destruction of the enemy too. That is what we just read in Isaiah 43.

“For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.” The same way he punishes our adversaries, he glorifies us. That is the bride of Christ: Christ is coming to get his woman. That is what the whole thing is about.

So the redeeming of Isaiah 43:1, “I have called thee by thy name”, is the calling of Wisdom 18: “us, whom thou hadst called”, glorified by the very judgment that punishes the nations holding us.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 16:14
precepts.why:
“I have redeemed thee.” Jeremiah shows that this redemption will be greater than the first: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.” When he delivered us out of Egypt, he destroyed Egypt, he destroyed Ethiopia and he destroyed Seba, Somalia.

“But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them.” The land of the north is North America. All the lands whither he had driven them are the Caribbean, Africa, and all the different lands we are scattered in.

“and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” That is Isaiah 43: “I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west.” We are here in the west, the western hemisphere.

So the redemption promised to Jacob is not the one out of ancient Egypt. It is the deliverance out of the land of the north and every land of our captivity, and it will be so great that the Exodus will no longer be what men speak of.

precepts.label: Romans 8:21
precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee.” Paul shows what that redemption brings: “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.”

The creature itself is you and me. We shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is talking about us being delivered, not just from this body, but from captivity.

It is the same promise as Jeremiah 16: the Lord that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands whither he had driven them, bringing them again into the land he gave their fathers. Isaiah 43 says he will say to the north, Give up, and bring his sons and daughters from the ends of the earth.

So “I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine” ends in liberty: the children of God set free from bondage, the captives delivered in the year of jubilee.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:26
precepts.why:
The Lord tells Jacob, “Fear not”, and promises, “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty.” Thirsty for what? Thirsty for the truth. Paul shows what that water is: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.” The water represents the word of God.

Read Isaiah with that in mind. “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”: I will pour the word of God upon them that are thirsty for the truth. “and floods upon the dry ground”: the floods also represent the word of God, poured out on the dry ground, these places wherein we dwell. “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring”: his spirit upon his people and his blessing upon their children.

God only chose Israel, and this washing is for his chosen, Jacob and Jesurun, “whom I have chosen.” The Lord made us and formed us from the womb, and he will help us.

When the word is poured out, “they shall spring up as among the grass.” That is what we are looking at now: the Israelites are waking up and springing up worldwide like grass. And verse 5 shows three kinds of Israelites waking up: one says “I am the Lord’s”, acknowledging we are the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; another takes on a new name and calls himself “by the name of Jacob”; another changes his surname and will “surname himself by the name of Israel.” It is the word of God, the water, that cleanses them and brings them back.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:23
precepts.why:
“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.” That does not mean there will be no sun and no moon. They will always be there. But we are not going to need that light, because we are going to be on another level: a spiritual level, a god level.

Revelation shows the same thing: “And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.” That is what we just read in Isaiah 60:19.

The city is “the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” That is what Christ meant when he said, Thy kingdom come. It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.”

“Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.” Everything goes back to the way it was. Israel in the kingdom lives in the light of the Lamb, and the days of our mourning are ended.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:24
precepts.why:
“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” People use this to say all the nations will be saved. But saved does not mean salvation here; it is in the context of rulership. Saved from what?

The precept is Zechariah: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Saved means left: they were left from being destroyed. Christ did not destroy them, and they are going to obey. Walking in the light of it means they serve the King and keep the feast of tabernacles.

“and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”, as Isaiah says: “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.”

“And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” Those nations do not walk in. They bring it to us at the front gate, and then they go back. Those written in the Lamb’s book of life are the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:3
precepts.why:
“Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” God is saying to us, Arise, wake up. Shine means teach. Thy light is come: Christ is come. The glory of the Lord risen upon thee is the Holy Spirit.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people.” We are in the worst darkness. “but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee”: wisdom and knowledge shall be seen upon us.

“And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.” The other nations shall come to our light. What is our light? The laws in Christ. And what does it look like for them to come to it? Zechariah 14: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Keeping the high holy days: that is them coming to our light.

That is why the Lord is our everlasting light in Isaiah 60:19. The nations do not bring the light; they come to Israel’s light and bring their kings and their wealth to it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:23
precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” This was brought up for the nations coming to Israel’s light in the kingdom.

The book, chapter and verse the Bishop was looking for is Zechariah 14, where it is spelled out: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” The nations that are left come up to worship at the appointed times, keeping the high holy days. That is them coming to our light.

So all flesh coming to worship is not all flesh entering the city. They are the nations left from destruction, serving and worshipping the King at his feasts, while only those written in the Lamb’s book of life, the twelve tribes of Israel, enter the city whose everlasting light is the Lord.

precepts.label: Luke 4:18
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 is fulfilled in Christ, who read it himself: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.” The good tidings of Isaiah are the gospel. And the poor are not everybody: “the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” The poor are the poor of Zion. You do not even have to go to Isaiah 14; Isaiah 61 itself says it is them that mourn in Zion.

“he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives.” We are the captives. How can you read captive and think everybody? Rome was dominating Israel at that time. “and recovering of sight to the blind”: we are the blind people. “to set at liberty them that are bruised”: bruised in sin.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.” The acceptable year of the Lord is our day of jubilee, and we had better accept that.

Imagine the Israelites and the Romans sitting in church together, the captives and the captors side by side, told we are all the same. It makes no sense. Jake looks over at Esau to see if he is upset, and if master is upset at this reading, he disregards it: black Christians hate anything that upsets white folks, and that is why they do not believe. But Christ read it plainly: he came to proclaim liberty to the captives of Israel, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound, bound in these prisons we call America, the Caribbean and whatever lands we are in.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:32
precepts.why:
“the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek.” Christ read it in Luke 4 as “to preach the gospel to the poor.” When it says the poor, who is that? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

That is telling you who the poor are: the poor of Zion, the poor of his people. Zion is another name for the Israelites.

And Isaiah 61 itself agrees: he came “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes”. Why are we mourning? Because we are captive.

So the good tidings, the brokenhearted, the captives and them that are bound are not all nations. They are the poor of the Lord’s people, the Israelites in captivity, who shall trust in the Zion the Lord has founded.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 3:19
precepts.why:
When the captives are set free, “ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord”, “For your shame ye shall have double”, and “their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” No matter where we go on this planet they are going to know our children by name. Today you want to talk to your boss and he turns his back to you; on that day they are going to beg for your attention.

Zephaniah is the precept to that: “Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee.” He is going to undo all the nations that afflict us. “and I will save her that halteth”: we are the ones that halt, because we are captive. “and gather her that was driven out.”

“and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame.” We get that fame and that glory, and our children are going to get it too. Everybody is going to acknowledge who we are. “At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the Lord.”

That is the liberty proclaimed to the captives in Isaiah 61: not only freed, but honoured in the very lands that shamed us.

precepts.label: Isaiah 63:4
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 proclaims “the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God.” There is a particular day in a particular year when God will come to deliver his people. Isaiah 63 shows that day: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?” This is Christ, the Son of God, and his garment is glorious, not a sheet or a robe.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Isaiah is asking Christ, Why are you red? It looks like you were stomping grapes. “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me.” Christ trod down the nations and killed them alone. He did not need the help of the twelve tribes of Israel; he did it himself.

“for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments.” The wine represents their blood.

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” We are the redeemed. The year of my redeemed is the acceptable year of the Lord in Isaiah 61, our jubilee, and it comes with the day of vengeance on the nations.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:41
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” That is slavery. It is a different thing from the servant of Leviticus 25, a poor Hebrew brother who sold himself to his brother for six years and went out free and furnished in the year of release. Christianity used the words servants, obey your masters, to make us think the Bible's servant was chattel slavery; it is not. Deuteronomy 28:41 is the captivity that came as the curse.

It is what Jeremiah 34 brought on us. Zedekiah made all the people covenant to let every Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free, “that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.” They obeyed, “But afterward they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return”. This is some negro stuff: the elites among us, those who had money, wanted to keep our own people in continuous servitude. So the Lord proclaimed a liberty for us “to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine”, to be “removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” That is Deuteronomy 28. Babylon had just left, and God brought them right back. That is the result of hating our brothers and not loving our neighbour as ourselves. Even after Persia set us free, in Nehemiah 5 the nobles did the same thing again.

After the Persian captivity came the Greek. 1 Maccabees 3:41: “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and “a power also of Syria and of the land of the Philistines joined themselves unto them.” We look at the slave auction and think it is the first time this ever happened. No, the Greeks did this too, and other nations helped them.

2 Maccabees 5 shows it: Jason, an Israelite, a treasonous negro, “slew his own citizens without mercy”, treating his countrymen like enemies to please the Greeks, and he died cast out, with none to mourn him. “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done” (Colossians 3:25). Then the king took the city: “fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.” Apollonius was sent “to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort”. The best age, the movers and shakers who make a nation thrive; take them and leave the old and feeble, and you destroy the nation, the same complaint made about the colonialists.

So the sons and daughters we begat went into captivity, sold by the Greeks, and after them by Rome, whose foothold came when Pompey captured Jerusalem in 65 BC, and the slave markets were full of black Jewish slaves. That is where breaking the year of release led.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 23:13-16
precepts.why:
When Ezekiel dug in the wall, he saw “every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” That is like putting the images of Cesare Borgia on the walls, or Guadalupe on the walls, today. Ezekiel 23 shows what they were putting on the walls: images of the gods of their enemies.

“Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea”. Israel looked at the pictures of her enemies on the wall, dressed up like princes.

“And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.” As soon as she saw them, she wanted them. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes you will go a whoring.

So the imagery on the walls of the temple in Ezekiel 8 was not harmless decoration. The images of other nations and their gods drew Israel's eyes, and her eyes drew her heart after them. It is the same today with the images hung on our walls, and it is why the Lord said, I cannot be around you all, and went far off from his sanctuary.

precepts.label: John 3:19
precepts.why:
Ezekiel was shown “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” Seventy elders with censers in their hands, burning incense to the images in the dark. What do they do in the dark? What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

Christ gives the judgment on it: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the dark because their deeds are evil; they hide there because they think the Lord does not see them.

But the Lord brought Ezekiel through the hole in the wall to show him exactly what was done in the dark. Nothing done in the chambers of imagery is hidden from him. The ancients said the Lord had forsaken the earth, but it was they who had forsaken the light, and that is the condemnation.
