precepts.label: Hebrews 8:10-11
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”. The rod is correction. And the bond of the covenant is the new covenant in Hebrews: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord”. After those days means after we are delivered out of here, out of this new Egypt, America.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. Meaning we are going to know God's laws and we will keep God's laws. Right now it can be routine: you go to work every day, stop in the donut store for a donut and your coffee, eat the donut, and then remember, damn, it's the days of unleavened bread, how could I forget? But the Lord God says his laws will be in our minds. We are not going to forget, and we will do them and serve him. That is the new covenant. We are in the beginning of it now, but once Christ returns it will be fully established in the wilderness.

“And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.” All of us will know the Lord, from the least amongst us to the greatest. You won't have to go and teach anybody, because the Lord is going to teach us. Every custom and thought we learned in America has to go, and he will show us even the parts we are missing now, like the sun and the moon working together for the times and seasons, wisdom destroyed from amongst us through slavery.

So being brought into the bond of the covenant is us being purged in the wilderness again. As he pleaded with our fathers and got rid of the leaven from amongst them, he will “purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”: those that break God's laws, those with leaven in them. Many will be delivered out of here, but not everyone is going to make it into the promised land. Those who enter will have his laws written in their hearts.

thread.label: Ezekiel 31:3
thread.text: Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches, and with a shadowing shroud, and of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Psalms 80:8
precepts.why:
Pharaoh is asked who he is like in his greatness, and the answer is the great cedar: “Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches.” The Lord speaks to the prophets by similitudes, saying one thing that means another, and here he compares the Egyptian kingdom to Adam's kingdom, Adam ruling, to give us more insight into what we read in Genesis. “The waters made him great”: the waters that came from the Father made Adam great, flowing from him through all his plants, all Adam's children. And “his boughs were multiplied.” What are the boughs that multiplied?

Asaph answers in Psalm 80, crying to the “Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock”: “Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it. Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land. The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars. She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river.”

Those boughs are Israel, the sons of God. All of this is talking about Israel: all of us that were drinking that water, and everybody was not getting that water like us. Isaiah says the same: “In that day shall the branch of the Lord be beautiful and glorious.” The branches of the Lord are Israel, those of us that escape the destruction and get the kingdom.

So the boughs multiplied on the great cedar are Adam's true children, Israel, and the same vine the Lord brought out of Egypt and planted is the vine that filled the land with its shadow in Adam's kingdom.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 17:23
precepts.why:
Ezekiel 31 says the great cedar was “of an high stature”, and “All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs.” The fowls of heaven are the angels: all the angels were under Adam when he was ruling, as it says, “let all the angels of God worship him.” Under his branches the beasts of the field brought forth their young, and the serpent was “more subtil than any beast of the field”: Satan was there, under Adam. And “under his shadow dwelt all great nations”, all the nations of the earth.

Ezekiel 17 shows the same cedar planted again: “I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent.” That is talking about Christ. “In the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing; in the shadow of the branches thereof shall they dwell.” That is the same as Ezekiel 31. He will plant it in the height of Israel, where it was before.

“And all the trees of the field shall know that I the Lord have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish.” He brought us down, and he raises us back up again. Ezra saw it too: on mount Sion, in the midst of a great people, “a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest.”

To understand the kingdom of Adam you have to understand the kingdom that is to come. It will be the same thing: us ruling with Christ in righteousness, with all the fowl dwelling under the goodly cedar, and nobody able to hurt us.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 2:24
precepts.why:
The great cedar was so fair that “all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.” The fir trees were not like his boughs, the chesnut trees not like his branches. His boughs and branches were his true children, his firstborn in the heavens, immortal and ruling with him. The other trees were the children Adam had on the earth before the fall, not created in his image, the multitude “born in vain.” They envied him, and they envied the twelve tribes that were with him.

Wisdom of Solomon shows who else envied him: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity. Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world.” The man God created was Adam. Adam was immortal and his sons were immortal; the children he had on the earth were created as men, sons of men, and were not immortal.

The devil also envied Adam. Satan went to war with Adam, and when he could not get him, he went through his woman to take him down: he jumped on his wife, played with her emotions and tricked her. Through the envy of Satan, that is how death came.

It will be the same in the future: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee.” When Christ returns and sets us back on this earth to rule, the nations will envy us, the same as back then, but they will not be able to do anything against us.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 31:14
precepts.why:
The great cedar that was lifted up in his height was driven out “for his wickedness”, and the Lord gives the end of it: “To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height, neither shoot up their top among the thick boughs, neither their trees stand up in their height, all that drink water: for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit.”

We are all delivered unto death. All that drank the water, his boughs, his branches, Israel, now have to come down on the earth and die as men. Before that we had our spiritual body, our angelic body. They go down “in the midst of the children of men” because they were not regular men. That goes back to “I have said, Ye are gods”, and “ye shall die like men.”

Read on: “In the day when he went down to the grave I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed.” The day Adam was cast out, the waters his boughs and branches were drinking were restrained. No water was coming to Adam anymore. Those great waters are the same living waters of Revelation 22; they stopped when Adam fell. Lebanon mourned for him and all the trees of the field fainted for him: his children.

“I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell.” Hell there is the grave, the earth. When Adam fell, the Lord withdrew paradise, a spiritual realm connected to the earth, and it caused devastation, and millions died, as Ezra says, “as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.” That is where Cain found his wife: not everybody died.

And “all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon”, Adam's top leaders, “shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth.” We are comforted here by the scriptures, “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

thread.label: Ezekiel 37:16-23
thread.text: Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the h

classes.title: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10-11
precepts.why:
When the voice told Peter, “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common”, Peter would have had to go to the Old Testament to explain what God had cleansed. He would go to Ezekiel 37: “I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” And whom was he gathering, and from where? “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen”: they were living among the Gentiles, the nations. He gathers them, cleanses them, and takes the two kingdoms, the stick of Judah and the stick of Joseph in the hand of Ephraim, and makes them one.

Hosea shows the same joining: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.” That is the two sticks becoming one in the Lord's hand.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The northern kingdom, cast out among the heathen and called not my people, would be called the sons of the living God again. That was the prophecy, and that is why Peter could not call those men common: the time had come, Peter, we have to gather them together, bring them together.

And guess what: that is happening now. It has been going on since back then until now. We are out in South America gathering God's people, out in Africa gathering God's people, and here in the States bringing God's people back together, Judah and Israel under one head.

thread.label: Daniel 7:4
thread.text: The first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings: I beheld till the wings thereof were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made stand upon the feet as a man, and a man’s heart was given to it.

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Revelation 13:2
precepts.why:
John saw “a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.” Blasphemy means wicked lies against God, and those lies are written on the heads of this beast. Then he describes it: “And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard, and his feet were as the feet of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion”. This is not the old kingdoms themselves; it is a beast rising in the last days that carries the attributes of all three.

The leopard is Greece. Daniel saw “another, like a leopard, which had upon the back of it four wings of a fowl; the beast had also four heads”. The four wings are four armies, the Greek military split four ways, and the four heads are the four generals: Ptolemy, Lysimachus, Cassander and Seleucus.

The bear is the Medo-Persian Empire. It “raised up itself on one side”: Persia rose up over the Medes and became the greater. The “three ribs in the mouth of it” are Egypt, Ethiopia and the Sabeans (that is Somalia), the three nations named in Isaiah 45:14: “The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature”. The same chapter opens, “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus”: God raised up Cyrus the Persian to conquer those three nations and take over the world.

The lion is Babylon, the first beast of Daniel 7:4, “like a lion, and had eagle’s wings”. The wings were plucked when Babylon put down Assyria. It was “made stand upon the feet as a man, and a man’s heart was given to it”: great wisdom was given to Babylon.

So the beast of Revelation 13 has elements of Greece, elements of Persia and Media, of Cyrus and those rulers, and the mouth of ancient Babylon. “and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority”: Satan gave this kingdom its power and great authority.

That is why the lion of Daniel 7:4 matters today. When you read about Babylon, Persia and Media and the Greeks, certain things in that history are being fulfilled in these last days. Everybody doesn't know that. And the head “wounded to death” is Rome, wounded in the year 193 AD.

thread.label: Daniel 7:25
thread.text: And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of t

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain
The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World
The Truth Behind Christmas and New Years

precepts.label: Genesis 1:14
precepts.why:
Revelation 13:5 says “there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies”, and Daniel 7:25 says the same: “he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High”. Revelation 13:7 adds that “it was given unto him to make war with the saints”. The great words are things like the image of Cesare Borgia as Christ, a white man dying for the sins of everybody on the planet, getting dumped in the water to be saved, Lent, Christmas, December 25th and the rest. To wear out the saints is slavery.

“and think to change times and laws”. They changed the time with daylight saving time. They moved the beginning of the year from spring to January. Genesis 1:14 was read to show something else they changed: “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”.

Leviticus 23 shows what the seasons are for: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” The Sabbath is listed first, and it is all year round. Then come the seasonal holidays: Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, in the spring; the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth; Pentecost, counting fifty days; the blowing of trumpets on the first day of the seventh month, the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth of the seventh month; and the feast of tabernacles on the fifteenth.

Sirach 43:6: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The declaration of times is the high holy days. The lights God set in the heaven keep his calendar, and that is the calendar the beast thought to change.

precepts.label: Genesis 1:16
precepts.why:
“And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.” The greater light is the sun and the lesser light is the moon. Notice the wording: great lights. He did not make a quarter moon or half a light. He made two great lights. What they call the full moon today is actually the new moon, and many cultures, like the Maya, hold full moon gatherings. Deuteronomy 33:14 speaks of Joseph's land and “the precious things put forth by the moon”, things that come out when the moon is at its peak, like the coquí frogs that come out under the moonlight in the islands where Ephraim and Manasseh dwell.

Sirach 43 goes on: “From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven”. The word month comes from moon. Every feast starts at the new moon in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom. The armies above are the armies of Revelation 19: “the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses”.

The moon is “a sign of the world”. The full moon stands for when we were in our full power and understanding. As it wanes and goes dark, that is us going into captivity, into full darkness, and when it comes back to fullness, that is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. Isaiah 60:2: “the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. When you see the dark moon, that is what it represents: we lost our heritage, and darkness covers the world.

Psalm 82 shows why: “How long will ye judge unjustly”, and because of it, “all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” Even the lights are out of course because of our sins. The seasons are out of order, and if the Sabbath comes every seven days, a month should have twenty-eight days. Isaiah 30:26 shows the kingdom: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases, so in the kingdom the moon will not go back into darkness. Binding up the breach is gathering the twelve tribes again, as Amos 9:11 says: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”.

thread.label: Daniel 9:24-27
thread.text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to sea

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Hebrews 1:9
precepts.why:
Christ told Peter to forgive seventy times seven, and Christ never put numbers out just to put them there. Seven represents completion, but what is seventy times seven? Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. That is 490 years, from Persia to Christ, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

Who is the most Holy that is anointed? Hebrews 1:9 explains it: “Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” That is talking about Christ. Where Daniel says “to anoint the most Holy”, that is Christ.

So the seventy weeks run “unto the Messiah the Prince”, which is Jesus Christ, and the reconciliation for iniquity and the end of sins come through him. The prophecy was 490 years, completing that perfection through Christ, because we needed that mercy. We couldn't sacrifice when we were enslaved under Babylon and Persia; we were always in captivity, going from one captivity to the next, so we needed Christ.

The apostles said it: “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel”. That is why he told Peter to forgive his brother seventy times seven: because he forgave us seventy times seven. He is that complete perfection. But don't take him for granted.

precepts.label: Luke 21:20
precepts.why:
“And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: cut off for the children of Israel. “and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”. That prince that shall come and destroy the sanctuary is Titus. “and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The flood is 70 AD, the destruction, and us being led away into captivity.

Christ spoke of that same desolation: “And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” What armies? The Roman armies. That is what Daniel 9:26 is speaking of, the prince that shall come and destroy the city and the sanctuary.

Then Daniel 9:27: “in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”: the temple being destroyed. “and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation”. The Roman armies around Jerusalem were the sign that the desolation determined in the seventy weeks was at hand.

So the 490 years end with Christ cut off for us and the desolation of the city by Titus. After that there was no sacrifice for us but Christ, and that is why his sacrifice is our only way through to perfection.

thread.label: Hosea 1:6
thread.text: And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And God said unto him, Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.

classes.title: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
Hosea's children were for signs. His daughter Lo-ruhamah means no mercy: “I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away”, which is Assyria overthrowing Ephraim so that it would be not a people. Then his son: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” When you are not God's people and he is not your God, what does that make you? A Gentile, a heathen, a stranger, a non-Israelite. Judah read this and said, good, the hell with Ephraim; they ain't his people no more, they're Gentiles, and we can't deal with them.

But Hosea goes straight on: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” When they were told they were Gentiles, it would be said to them, no, you are not Gentiles; you are God's people.

Judah forgot this. Judah said, you guys are Gentiles forever. But Hosea says eventually you have to come together again: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”. That one head is Christ, and they are delivered together, united as one. Chapter 2 says the same: “I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.” Judah just took a black highlighter and covered that part, because they were evil and stupid.

The same thing is in Chronicles. The northern kingdom was “without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law”, because Jeroboam set up idols in Dan and Shiloh so they would not go south to worship in Jerusalem. That is why they were called strangers: King Asa “gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” Whenever Judah was on point, Ephraim came in. The Lord always uses Judah to bring Ephraim back, and the strangers, the not my people, turn out to be the sons of the living God.

thread.label: Hosea 12:10
thread.text: I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 9:15
precepts.why:
Solomon shows why man cannot understand the things above by himself: “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” And hardly do we guess aright at the things that are upon earth, let alone the things that are in heaven.

Ezra wanted to know the things above the heavens and asked the angel to give him understanding. Did the angel reveal a lot of things in heaven to Ezra? Yes. So, in order to understand spiritual things, things on another level, the Lord has to reveal them to you.

That is why the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” Our corruptible body presses the soul down, and we read with an earthly, carnal mind. The things Moses was shown on the mount, the secrets of the times and the end, were hidden in similitudes, and it takes the Lord's spirit coming into you to show you what they mean.

precepts.label: Job 11:6
precepts.why:
Moses was held on the mount a long season and told many wondrous things, the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded, “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” How did Moses hide them? Hosea says the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude is a likeness, a resemblance, a comparison, like a metaphor: you speak of a tree, but you are not really talking about a tree. When Genesis speaks of the trees in the garden, it is comparing trees to human beings. It is all going into Adam's kingdom, but it is hidden.

Job calls those hidden things the secrets of wisdom: “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The secrets of wisdom are the things Moses hid.

And they are double. You read a scripture, but it is not saying only one thing; it is saying two things. Many times we read a scripture and think we have it, then read it again and the Most High takes us to see something else on another level. That doesn't make what we first saw wrong; there is simply another level to it.

The Lord told Moses to hide these things because they are not meant for everybody to understand. But today some will understand them, because the Lord “revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.”

thread.label: Amos 4:5
thread.text: And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord God.

classes.title: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

precepts.label: Matthew 16:6
precepts.why:
Amos rebukes Israel: “offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel”. Christ shows what that leaven is: “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees”.

The leaven of the Pharisees was hypocrisy; the leaven of the Pharisees is sin. Christ is saying, be careful of the sins of the Pharisees, for they say and do not. So the leaven in the scriptures is really going into sin, and leaven is not only bread with yeast in it; it is something much more symbolic.

That is what Amos exposes. We were offering our thanksgiving with leaven, with sin, and thinking that was acceptable to God. You cannot be in the midst of sin and give God thanks offerings. The Lord said, I don't work with that, I don't deal with that. That's how you black people is: in the midst of sin and coming to me with offerings.

So the days of unleavened bread we are celebrating represent us being without sin. The soul that has leaven in it for those seven days is cut off, and that is damnation. It is going into something much heavier: the days of unleavened bread are us fixing ourselves right now, getting rid of the leaven, the sins you are battling, trying to become a better person, so that when the Lord returns our souls are not cut off.

thread.label: Amos 5:5
thread.text: But seek not Beth–el, nor enter into Gilgal, and pass not to Beer–sheba: for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity, and Beth–el shall come to nought.

classes.title: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.label: Jeremiah 7:12
precepts.why:
Amos warns Ephraim, “seek not Beth–el, nor enter into Gilgal”, for “Beth–el shall come to nought.” These were places built for worship by Abraham and Jacob, and Ephraim turned them into seats of idolatry. So Gilgal would surely go into captivity, and Beth–el would be destroyed. “Seek the Lord, and ye shall live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph”: the house of Joseph is Ephraim.

Jeremiah turns the same judgment on Judah: “But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.” Go look at Shiloh and see what I did to it. “I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not”: they refused the prophets.

“Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh. And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.” What was done to Ephraim will be done to Judah: the heathen come in, destroy the sanctuary and lead them captive. The exact same way. The same thing happens to both houses, both kingdoms. He raised up Assyria to overthrow Ephraim, and he raised up Babylon to overthrow Judah.

And they would not hear it. Amaziah the priest of Bethel, one of the low-level priests raised up that was not Levi, told Amos, “go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel”. Go teach Judah; you are disturbing the king's church. Amos was blitzing the churches. But the Lord said to him, “Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.” The Lord always sent his prophets to his people, and his people alone, to repent. It is the same with Jacob today: the one preaching the word of God is called a troublemaker.

So Bethel came to nought as Shiloh did, and Israel went “into captivity forth of his land”: their wives made harlots, their sons and daughters fallen by the sword, their land divided by line as it is to this day, dying “in a polluted land”. That began with the northern kingdom, but eventually it happened to all of us as a whole.

thread.label: Obadiah 1:19
thread.text: And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: Joshua 15:21
precepts.why:
Before Obadiah, the class read Jeremiah 50:19: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” To know whose land Carmel and Bashan were, go back to the first dividing of the land in Joshua. Write it down: Carmel was Judah's.

Joshua 15 gives the cities of Judah: “And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward were Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,” “And Kinah, and Dimonah”. Then jump to verse 55: “Maon, Carmel, and Ziph”. Those belonged to Judah. Judah's lot ran to the south, right up against the coast of Edom.

Jeremiah 50 goes on to say what God will do when he brings us back: “the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.” He wipes away our iniquity and brings us again to our own habitation.

Then watch how things get switched around. Obadiah says “they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau.” The mount of Esau is where Edom used to dwell originally, and we are going to take that whole area. “and they of the plain the Philistines”: we are going to take Palestine. We shall possess the fields of Ephraim and the fields of Samaria. The land is ours by inheritance from the first dividing, and when God brings Israel back it will be possessed even further than it was then.

precepts.label: Joshua 13:29
precepts.why:
Jeremiah 50:19 says Israel “shall feed on Carmel and Bashan”. Carmel was Judah's; now Bashan. Joshua 13 shows it: “And Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh: and this was the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families.” “And their coast was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair”. Bashan belonged to Manasseh.

Read Jeremiah 50:19 again so you get the thought: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” God is bringing Israel back to the very lands the tribes were given at the beginning.

Now see how it gets switched around in Obadiah. “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.” Benjamin shall possess Gilead. The tribes come back to the land, but the land is shared out anew.

Verse 20 goes on: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”. The land of the Canaanites is the land of Israel, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Sepharad is the Asia Minor region and Spain. Our people scattered there come home and take the cities of the south.

precepts.label: Zechariah 10:10
precepts.why:
Obadiah said “Benjamin shall possess Gilead”, and Zechariah shows God bringing us there: “I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead”. He is going to take us out of captivity and bring us into the land of Gilead. That is Obadiah 19 that was just read.

Then “and Lebanon”. Who belongs in Lebanon? Go back to Obadiah verse 20: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Then verse 21: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau”, the mount of Edom.

Then “and place shall not be found for them.” There is not going to be enough room for us. Isaiah 49 says the same: “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”. There will be too many of us. “and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away”: the nations that swallowed us up shall be far away.

Then: “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” This place is too narrow; make room for me. That is why Christ said that in his Father's house are many mansions. Israel will come back in such numbers that the land cannot hold us.

precepts.label: Zechariah 13:8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 49:20 speaks of “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”. The ones we lost are the two thirds, here in America. In case somebody asks what that means, Zechariah shows it: “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.”

Notice it says in all the land. The land it is talking about is Babylon, and that is America. So two out of every three Israelites shall die here in America. The ones we lost are them wicked Israelites.

Then the third: “And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

That remnant is who goes back to possess the land in Obadiah. And even after the two thirds are gone, the children that are left shall say, “The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” The land will still be too narrow for the ones God brings back.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:12
precepts.why:
Zephaniah says, “for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride”. Who rejoices in our pride? Sirach proves what pride is: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”.

Pride is departing from God, going against his commandments; it is our sin. So those that rejoice in our pride are the ones that rejoice in us going against God's commandments: the pastors, the Christians, the churches, the Democrats and the Republicans. They rejoice in us not keeping God's commandments. The Lord says, I am going to take them out of you, take them away from you, “and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain”, the land of Israel.

What he leaves is “an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the Lord.” The elect beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, the daughter of his dispersed, a large portion of them on the continent of Africa, are afflicted and very poor, as we saw going throughout Africa keeping Passover and the feast of unleavened bread. They must be taught to trust in the name of the Lord.

“The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies”, because they are being taught the commandments, and that is what we go out there for. No, Jesus is not white; no, he was not born December 25th; no, we are not to pray to Mary or to the ancestors. Sin has always been the problem, and breaking God's commandments is a sign of unbelief. When the ones who rejoice in our departing from God are taken away, the remnant shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.

thread.label: Zechariah 2:6-8
thread.text: Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.

classes.title: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.label: Psalms 78:68
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “come forth, and flee from the land of the north”: flee from North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: all Israel scattered, like we read in Matthew 24 and James 1. Then he singles out one group: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.”

Many scriptures tell us that Zion represents the twelve tribes. But in this context, which Zion is it? Asaph answers: “But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” That is the Zion right there.

So “Deliver thyself, O Zion” is talking about Judah: deliver yourself, Judah. That does not mean all the Judahites are in the land of the north; Judah was dispersed like all the other tribes. But God is pinpointing a particular group of Judah that would be in the land of the north, dwelling with the daughter of Babylon.

That fits the rest of the prophecy. In these last days the Lord raises up Judah first: the Lord “shall save the tents of Judah first”, and the blessing of Judah is, “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people.” The voice of Judah is the teaching of Judah, carried to the other eleven tribes.

precepts.label: Psalms 137:7-8
precepts.why:
Zechariah says Zion, Judah, “dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” The key is who the daughter of Babylon is. The psalm names her: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” The word rase means destroy it: destroy it even to the foundation.

Then the very next words: “O daughter of Babylon.” Notice what it is calling them now. It is calling Edom, the so-called white folks, the daughter of Babylon.

So the scripture lets you know Judah would live among Edom, and where? In the land of the north. That is why the Lord cries, “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north.” The group of Judah in North America is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon, the children of Edom who wanted Jerusalem razed to the ground.

And the Lord's word to that people is: “he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” We are God's favorite, and the nations which spoiled us will answer for it.

thread.label: Matthew 1:21
thread.text: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: John 1:29
precepts.why:
We did not return to what the Most High commanded, the feasts he told us to go back to, and that is why we were in need of a saviour, an ultimate sacrifice. From Abraham to David, from David to the carrying away into Babylon, and from Babylon to Christ were fourteen generations each; we were always in slavery.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His name means he saves. His people: the Israelites only. From their sins. That is why he was the ultimate sacrifice.

His cousin John expounds on it: “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” The Lamb of God. Christ was that perfect, ultimate sacrifice, the lamb that takes away the sins of the people he came to save.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:5-8
precepts.why:
To expound further on Christ being the ultimate sacrifice: “Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me”. The body was Christ. The sacrificial laws of animal sacrifice were a preparation for what was to come, a shadow of good things to come; the good thing that came was the body of Jesus Christ, dying only for the nation of Israel.

“In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.” The Most High had no pleasure in those sacrifices. They were temporary, to train us and prepare us for Christ.

“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” In the volume of the book: the whole book, not just the New Testament. Christ is present in the Old Testament, and Christ is present before the Old Testament.

“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law”. So the offerings of the law pointed to the body prepared for him, the one sacrifice that saves his people from their sins.

precepts.label: John 1:3
precepts.why:
Christ was always the plan. He is the author, the executive producer, whatever title you want to give him. From before the Old Testament, the body prepared for him in the volume of the book was the plan for saving his people from their sins.

John shows it: “All things were made by him”. All things were made by Christ: the principalities, the things you see out in space, the worlds, with an s. “And without him was not any thing made that was made.”

The one who made all things is the one who came as the Lamb of God to save his people. The sacrifices of the law, the seventh day and the rest it points to were all his from the beginning. So when the angel said “thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins”, it was the Maker of all things coming to fulfil the plan that was always his.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:1
precepts.why:
Matthew writes “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”, and Isaiah had already written it: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

Matthew says “Galilee of the Gentiles”; Isaiah says “Galilee of the nations.” So the nations also means the Gentiles. Same land, same people, same word.

What we read in Matthew 4:15 was already recorded in the Old Testament. When the apostles and prophets spoke, they had to substantiate their points from what we call the Old Testament today. Whatever they said, they had to be able to justify it with that text. Matthew is not saying something new; he is showing the prophecy fulfilled.

This is the foundation for Acts 10. By the biblical text the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles, like strangers, like heathens. The New Testament shows Paul going out to find them scattered among the nations and bring them back to God, because the prophecy sent from the Old Testament was that the job was to raise up the 12 tribes of Israel again. The Gentiles of Galilee are Israelites that were scattered and cut off, and God is gathering them back.

precepts.label: Acts 11:19
precepts.why:
“Go not into the way of the Gentiles”: in this verse that includes the other eleven tribes. “And into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”: that is the Northern Kingdom. Why? Because it was not their time yet. The Lord said he would raise the tents of Judah first. “But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: that starts with Judah first.

Some are confused and think this is new. It is not; it has always been taught. Acts shows the order being followed after Christ: “Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.”

To none but the Jews only: only to Judah. They were primarily dealing with Judah first.

That does not mean the rest were never to be reached. Christ himself went to Samaria in John 4 and taught the Samaritans for a few days, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them. Judah first, and then the other tribes.

precepts.label: Romans 9:24
precepts.why:
The disciples went first to Judah, “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” Then watch what Paul says: “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?”

“Even us”: the tribe of Benjamin and all the other tribes. “Whom he hath called, not of the Jews only”: not of Judah only. “But also of the Gentiles”: the other eleven tribes.

Some were perverting Zechariah 12:7, where the Lord raises the tents of Judah first, as if it meant only Judah. Judah first is the order, not the whole. So go back to Matthew 10 with a better understanding: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” In the beginning it was Judah first; afterward the call went to the rest of the tribes. There is no contradiction once you know the order.

thread.label: Matthew 16:6
thread.text: Then Jesus said unto them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: Matthew 23:1-3
precepts.why:
Christ said, “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” What was the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees? Matthew 23 shows the first part of it.

“The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” They were hypocrites. What they said out of Moses' seat was the law, and that you do. But their works did not match their words.

“Do not ye after their works”, because their works were after someone else, and that is the rest of the leaven: who their works followed. The Passover reminds us that we were delivered because we were unleavened, righteous; so to be delivered again we have to move in the same spirit and purge the leaven out, not just check the box on the physical bread.

precepts.label: Mark 8:15
precepts.why:
Christ warned in Matthew 16 to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and in Matthew 23 he said to do what they bid from Moses' seat, but not after their works. Whose works were they following? Mark tells it: “And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.”

The leaven of Herod. That lets you know whose manner they were following: they were following the white man, Esau. That is why he tells us to beware.

So their leaven was not just being hypocrites. They were following after the manner of the wicked. Leaven is an influence that spreads, and when the rulers of Israel took on Herod's leaven, it spread through them; they came to move in the same spirit as the wicked they served. That is the warning to us: do not take on the leaven of Herod, the spirit of Esau, while wearing the garments of Israel.

precepts.label: John 11:45-48
precepts.why:
John 11 shows the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod at work. “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They believed on Christ.

“But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.” Wherever there is good, evil has to be there. You had the believers, and then you had coons set up there, running to tell.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” The Romans. That lets you know who their masters were and who they were following after. That is the leaven of Herod.

Leaven is an influence that spreads. That bitterness is on the inside, and it corrupts the spirit, the same bitterness that was in Cain toward Abel. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead to keep their place under Rome. If you are bitter toward your brother, you are in the same position as the scribes and Pharisees: the same spirit.

thread.text: From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.

precepts.label: Luke 4:13
precepts.why:
Christ told the disciples he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and be raised again the third day. That was a good thing: he had to die to redeem the nation of Israel. But Peter took him and rebuked him: “Be it far from thee, Lord”. And Christ turned and said, “Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me”. What happened there? Satan literally jumped on Peter. That was not Peter; that was Satan talking to Christ through Peter, and Christ was talking to Satan.

Luke shows how that could be. After the temptation in the wilderness: “And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.” For a season. You think Satan stopped tempting Christ? He never stopped. He just left for a season and kept coming in different ways. When Christ was about to be crucified, Satan came back, and he came by jumping on Peter.

That is why Christ told Peter in another place that Satan desired to have him, to sift him as wheat, but that he had prayed for him that his faith fail not.

Satan comes for all of us; that is his job. For some it is money, for some it is sex, for some it is hatred. He comes at your weakness. So examine yourself: what is my weakness? That is what you need to strengthen, because that is what Satan will try to destroy you with. The worst are the ones who say they have no weakness; they deal with the heaviest demons and are just good at hiding it. The war is in your mind: when the evil thought comes, rebuke it, as Christ did: get thee behind me.

thread.label: Matthew 18:21-22
thread.text: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Luke 17:3-4
precepts.why:
Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance, the perpetual hatred Esau carries against his brother Jacob. Now the flip side: Peter asked, “Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” Christ answered, “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” Christ offers boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to do the same.

Luke gives the terms: “Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.” That brother is the children of thy people, as Leviticus 19:17 says. It is rebuke first, then repentance, then forgiveness.

“And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.” Why? Seven represents completion. The same way Christ forgave us when we were without sacrifice and without mercy: all our adulteries, fornication, lying and stealing during Assyria, Babylon, Persia and America, scattered in Africa in the dark ages doing all sorts of wicked things. Christ forgave all of that. That is why he said seventy times seven.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:12-13
precepts.why:
“Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness”, the mercy Christ offers us, “humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering”: longsuffering toward the brother who repents. “Forbearing one another”, as Christ forbears us, “and forgiving one another”.

Forgiving is something some of us need to pray for. Some can forgive nothing and hold on to grudges like there is no tomorrow. Imagine if Christ held on to grudges against us. We would not be here; we would be in hell with white Jesus, Islam and our sins. The only reason we are here is Jesus Christ and his boundless mercy toward us.

“If any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” Christ does not put numbers out just to put them. Seventy times seven is 490, and Daniel's seventy weeks, 490 years from Persia to Christ, were determined “to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity” through the Messiah cut off for the children of Israel. We could not sacrifice in Babylon and Persia; we needed Christ, the complete perfection of mercy. He forgave us seventy times seven, so we forgive our brother the same, and we do not take him for granted.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
People say the people in the land of Israel today are the Jews. That is not what the Bible says. After the tribulation, when the stars fall (the missiles) and the powers of the heavens are shaken (nations warring against each other), “he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Notice the angels do not go to one land to gather this people. Christ is letting us know the Israelites would not be in a land; they would be scattered worldwide.

Who is the elect? Some say anybody who worships. Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. That is the elect: Israel, scattered in the four winds from one end of heaven to the other.

Before the angels come for them, the Lord calls to the heavens and to the earth: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” The saints are “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”, and only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. The call to the heavens is to the angels; the call to the earth is to us.

So the message for us on earth is the same as the angels' commandment: gather the saints. We are not supposed to be looking for other races and nationalities, only the twelve tribes of Israel, scattered worldwide, which is why the gospel has to go out to every land.

thread.text: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.

classes.title: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.label: John 1:29
precepts.why:
At the Passover dinner Christ took the cup and said, “For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” The blood the Israelites put on the doorposts in ancient Egypt represented Christ's blood. It represented the new covenant: Christ coming and dying for our sins.

John shows who the lamb is: “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God”. Christ is called the Lamb of God. That male lamb of the first year represents Christ. He is that sacrifice.

So we do not sacrifice anymore, but we do have the dinner, with the understanding that the lamb represents Christ. Do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today; some brothers are crazy. Killing a lamb is not going to protect you from the wrath of God. Believing in Christ and doing what is right is what protects you from the wrath of God.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
The bread represents Christ's body, and the cup his blood “shed for many for the remission of sins.” Paul says it plainly: “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

Christ is our passover. The lamb that was killed represents Christ, and that is saying a lot. He was sacrificed for us; he came and died for our sins.

So you do not have to go kill a lamb and put the blood over the doorpost so that you do not die. You believe in Christ and you keep the commandments, and we come together, we break bread and we drink wine, as Christ did with the twelve at the Passover. That is being under the new covenant.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 16:16
precepts.why:
Luke says Mary “laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.” The inn is a hotel. Why was there no room in the hotels? Deuteronomy 16:16 shows it: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles”.

The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover; the feast of weeks is Pentecost. Three times a year all Israel had to go up to Jerusalem, and at that time every inn was full because everybody came up for the feast. There was no room in the inn because it was the Passover.

Christ was not born in the manger. The prophecy in Song of Solomon 8:5 says, “I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth”. Mary brought him forth under the apple tree, and after that took him to the manger, because the city was full for the feast.

precepts.label: Luke 2:8
precepts.why:
“And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.” The shepherds were out in the field with the flock at night. That does not happen in the winter.

A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime the animals are brought into the barn to stay warm; nobody is abiding in the field then. Around tabernacles, the ingathering, is when they bring in all their animals and all the crops to prepare for the mean season. So shepherds in the field by night fits the springtime, and Christ was born in the springtime, at the Passover.

Christmas has nothing to do with Christ. Do not give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you away from the truth; that is what Christmas does, it turns you away from the truth and from serving God.

precepts.label: Matthew 2:1
precepts.why:
“Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem”. East of Jerusalem is Babylon and the lands of the different captivities. Those wise men were Israel, living in the lands east of Jerusalem, “Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.”

The star they saw was a chariot, a light, what they call UFOs today, not a celestial body in the night sky. A planet cannot do what this did: “the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.” It guided them on the earth and stood over the house.

“And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother”. The house, not the manger. Christians show the wise men in a barn giving gifts to a baby, but time had passed; Christ was a young child now, a toddler of around two, walking and forming words. The wise men had been following that star at least two years. They were not three men; three is the number of the gifts, “gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.” They came as a caravan. With those gifts Christ was taken care of; he was not poor.

Herod, an Edomite who converted to being a Jew, a white man set up as king of Judea by Rome, “slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.” Thousands of black babies. That shows the child was around two when the wise men came. And when you see the synagogues of Satan killing babies in Palestine today, it does not surprise us; that is in their nature.

precepts.label: Luke 2:41
precepts.why:
“Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.” “And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast.” When did Christ turn twelve? At the Passover. Christ was born on the Passover and he died on the Passover.

When is the Passover? Leviticus 23:5: “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.” The fourteenth at evening is the fifteenth day, and that is when Christ was born: Abib, the first month, not December 25th.

1 Corinthians 5:7: “For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ is our Passover. That is why the inn was full when he was born: all Israel was up in Jerusalem for the feast.

December 25th goes back to the 25th of Kislev, when Antiochus IV Epiphanes desecrated the temple, set up Zeus and swine's flesh, and forced our people to worship Greek gods. God has festival days and Satan does too: we have our dedication and Satan has Christmas; we have our Passover and Satan has Easter. Stop giving heed to Jewish fables and following St. Nicholas and the Pope; that lie turns you away from the truth.

precepts.label: Hosea 4:17
precepts.why:
The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” These Samaritans were Israelites who still lived there. Samaria is north of Jerusalem, as the map shows, and the Jews of Jerusalem stopped dealing with our people located in Samaria.

Why did that happen? A brother answered from Hosea: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” That is why she said it. The scripture said Ephraim was joined to idols, and the word was to let him alone.

So the separation between the Jews and the Samaritans was not just a grudge; it grew out of the judgment on the northern kingdom for its idolatry. Judah took that word and left Ephraim alone. Yet here Christ, of Judah, sits at Jacob's well and asks a woman of Samaria to give him drink.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:6-11
precepts.why:
Hosea shows why Ephraim was let alone. “Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” He would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, because they fully went into idolatry. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen”, as can be read in 2 Kings 19.

“Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” That was the message to the northern kingdom because of his anger at their idolatry: you will not be my people, and I will not be your God. That is why the woman said the Jews have no dealings with us.

But then it comes back: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” What is he saying? I am going to bring you back together again.

All the prophets spoke from a place of prophecy, judgment, and eventually redemption. That is what gives us hope to change and repent. If there were no endgame where we come out of this, there would be no incentive. But God said if you turn back to me, in the place where it was said you are not my people, there you will be called the sons of God.

precepts.label: Isaiah 7:8
precepts.why:
Before Hosea recorded the Lord casting off the house of Israel, Isaiah had already prophesied it: “For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

They already knew. God already told them that within sixty-five years Ephraim, the northern kingdom, would be broken and destroyed, and that is what Hosea 1 is recording: Lo–ruhamah, no more mercy on the house of Israel, and Lo–ammi, ye are not my people.

So when the woman of Samaria says the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans, she is standing at the end of that prophecy. Ephraim was broken “that it be not a people”, cut off for idolatry. And that is exactly why it matters that Christ, a Jew, is speaking to her at Jacob's well: the people who were broken off are about to be offered the living water.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:26
precepts.why:
Christ told her, “If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” What is the living water? A brother answered from Ephesians: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”.

You are cleansed by the washing of water by the word, so the living water is the word of God. What Christ would have given her was understanding: the understanding that the tribes were going to be gathered back together again.

She said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? That shows she understood she was part of the twelve tribes of Israel; she just knew the Jews had no dealings with them. And Christ answered, “Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst”. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they had been disconnected from it for so long.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:23-29
precepts.why:
The water Christ gives is “a well of water springing up into everlasting life”, and Paul shows what that understanding is. He is a minister of the gospel “which was preached to every creature which is under heaven”, to fulfil the word of God: “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints”.

It was hid for ages that the northern kingdom had a part to play in this, to repent and come back. The ones who did understand were the learned men who studied, many of them the Pharisees, which is why they said, will he go to the dispersed among the Gentiles and teach them? They read Isaiah, Ezekiel and Deuteronomy. The masses didn't have the scriptures; the learned men had the parchment. But now he gave it to the apostles to teach.

“To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory”. The riches of this mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom has an opportunity of repentance: he is gathering back the Gentiles. The secret hid for ages is being revealed to the whole world; it is no longer gatekept. The apostles would go throughout the earth and teach the people that you are not Puerto Rican, you are not Dominican, whatever byword was given to you: you are the children of Israel. “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom”.

That is what is happening to us now. The understanding of this Bible and of who we are was hid for ages, but the Lord said in this hour the true worshippers are going to wake up.

precepts.label: Hosea 4:17
precepts.why:
Christ “must needs go through Samaria”, to Sychar, “near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph”, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh. The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The Samaritans were the northern kingdom, and the Jews had no dealings with them because of that beef from way back.

Hosea is where it came from: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” The Lord said leave them alone, they're joined to idols, and Judah took that as okay: what the hell with them, they're cast off. But Judah forgot the part where it said they would be joined together and appoint themselves one head. That was dismissed because of the hatred the houses had for each other, that back and forth.

Yet the woman said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? She called Jacob our father, and Joseph's house got that well: she was Israel. She said “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”, Gerizim, where all Israel worshipped before Jerusalem. And Isaiah said “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”, so she said “I know that Messias cometh”.

The disciples “marvelled that he talked with the woman”, because the Jews didn't deal with the northern kingdom. But those are our people. Christ taught the Samaritans two days, and they knew “that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world”: the world is Israel. The dividing hatred said let him alone, but Christ came to heal it.

precepts.label: Joshua 8:30-35
precepts.why:
The woman at the well said, “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. On the map, the mountains above the well are Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. Joshua 8 shows why she said it: “Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron: and they offered thereon burnt offerings unto the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings.” “And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.”

When we first came into the land, the first place we came into was what would be called Samaria, and the first altars were set up in Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. That is why, when the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up top and worshipped there: this is the place where we worshipped initially. But God called his home Jerusalem; that is where he set up his temple.

Read on: “And all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”. The blessings went up on the children of Israel, and the cursing was on Mount Ebal.

“There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.” When we came into the land we had a mixed multitude of the other nations among us, and they were conversant in the laws of God. They had to learn the laws. We taught them how to keep the Sabbath day: six days you do your work, and on the seventh no work, neither your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor the stranger that is within thy gates.

Then Christ answered her: “Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” There was a time coming, 70 AD, when Jerusalem would be toppled by the Romans, and neither the mountains of Samaria nor Jerusalem would matter, because he was destroying it. His purpose was to gather in one the twelve tribes of Israel.
