thread.label: Romans 5:12-21
thread.text: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

classes.title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 3:5-27
precepts.why:
“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men”. Yes, it passed upon all men; all nations are capable of sinning. The question is who God held accountable. Ezra tells the story. God “gavest a body unto Adam”, breathed into him the breath of life, and “unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” The evil in Adam passed into all nations; Cain and them were wicked by default.

But out of Adam came a specific line God wanted to keep his laws. The flood came, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men”: not Ham’s or Japheth’s line, but Shem’s, the righteous line of Seth. They multiplied and “began again to be more ungodly than the first”, so God chose Abraham: “Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will”. Judith shows Abraham’s people left the gods of their fathers in Chaldea and worshipped the God of heaven. God promised “that thou wouldest never forsake his seed”, and “As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau”. There is always that special line God deals with.

At Sinai he gave “the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel. And yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart”. “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” The same evil that was in Adam passed on to the righteous line. Then David built the city, and “they that inhabited the city forsook thee, And in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done: for they also had a wicked heart: And so thou gavest thy city over into the hands of thine enemies.”

It is a repeated cycle from Adam to Noah to Abraham to now: the righteous line gets God’s laws, goes against them, destruction comes, they repent, and out of that line the righteous rise again. The accountability for sin fell on that line. That is what Paul does in Romans 5: he gives the origin story of sin, how it killed off the chosen people, and why Christ had to come and die for that same chosen line.

precepts.label: Romans 8:29-30
precepts.why:
“So by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.” Who are the many? Romans 8 answers: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.” Foreknow means knew before. Before Adam was made, God knew the nation he would justify and glorify through his Son.

“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”. The called are the elect Peter wrote to, the strangers scattered throughout Galatia and the rest, “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”, “a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation”.

“And whom he called, them he also justified”: justified through the blood of Christ. “And whom he justified, them he also glorified”: as Isaiah says, “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

Amos says it plainly: “You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.” All nations sin, but God acknowledges only Israel’s sins and sent Christ for them. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” The free gift unto justification of life came upon the people God foreknew.

precepts.label: Ephesians 1:1-5
precepts.why:
Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”, the same saints as at Rome. Who are the saints? “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” No other nation made a covenant with God by sacrifice.

“According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”. As Eve was in Adam, we the bride were in Christ, chosen before the world was founded, “that we should be holy and without blame before him in love”.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. The adoption is the reconciliation, the atonement, the justification and the restoration.

So the many made righteous by the obedience of one in Romans 5 are the saints God chose in Christ before the foundation of the world. Adam’s offence brought death on the chosen line, and Christ’s obedience brings them back into the adoption that was always theirs.

precepts.label: Romans 11:1-2
precepts.why:
If sin reigned unto death over the chosen line, has God given up on them? Paul answers: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

“God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” Which he foreknew: that is Amos 3 and Romans 8 again. “You only have I known of all the families of the earth”, and “whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate”.

The cycle Ezra described, the righteous line receiving the law, going off, being destroyed and repenting, never ended with God throwing his people away. Every time, out of that line the righteous rose up again.

So where sin abounded, grace did much more abound, and it abounded upon the same people God foreknew. Paul, an Israelite of Benjamin, is himself the proof that God has not cast away his people.

precepts.label: Romans 9:3-5
precepts.why:
Paul’s heart is for his own: “For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh”. His kinsmen according to the flesh: his race. “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”.

Pertaineth means belongs. The adoption belongs to them, the adoption of Ephesians 1:5. The glory belongs to them: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob all belong to the Israelites.

“Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.”

Christ came for Israel. The free gift that came “upon all men unto justification of life” in Romans 5 is the adoption, the glory and the promises that pertain to the Israelites, the people whose sins God held to account from Adam on and whom he justified by the obedience of one.

thread.label: Romans 8:17
thread.text: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Revelation 2:26
precepts.why:
In Psalms 2 the Father says to Christ, “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” Christ is going to inherit all these nations and rule the planet.

All that Christ was given, we share, because we are “joint-heirs with Christ”. That is what a joint heir is: what Christ gets, he is going to give to us. Here is the proof: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”.

This is what we read in Psalms 2 that Christ is going to get, but because we are joint heirs, we are going to get it too. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.” The same honor and glory the Father gave to Christ, Christ says, I am going to give you that same power.

All we have to do, brothers, is endure to the end. “If so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together”: he that overcometh and keepeth his works unto the end is the one who receives power over the nations.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:6
precepts.why:
Psalms 2 goes on after the Father gives Christ the heathen for his inheritance: “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings”. Who are these kings? Revelation shows you: Christ “hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father”.

That is a message to us, advice and a command: be wise, O ye kings. “Be instructed, ye judges of the earth.” Christ is calling us judges of the earth. We might look like knuckles right now, but just give us time.

Paul says the same thing: “Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” And the saints are not everybody who believes on Jesus: “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. The saints are the Israelites, and the Israelites will judge this planet. Christ said the twelve that followed him “shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

So being heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ means being made kings and priests, the rulers and judges of the earth with him. If that is our future, Paul asks, why can we not judge the smallest matters among ourselves now? Be wise, be instructed, and endure.

precepts.label: Daniel 11:39
precepts.why:
“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?” How can our people call on the Almighty God that loves them when they have not believed in that God? Our people have believed in a strange god, a Eurocentric god. We are the only race that has a god that does not look like us. The God we serve is not the same God as the white man.

Daniel shows it: “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory”. That white Jesus is a strange god. “And he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain.” The white man divided Africa for gain. That is what the Bible says he did.

Why is that god strange? Because he does not look like you. He has no laws, statutes or commandments. And he whooped you in slavery. We know that was the white man, yet we run on Sunday morning and pray faithfully to the same white man that shot us down in the streets and raped our mothers and fathers. Strange god.

“And how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?” Because we have been following a strange god all our lives, someone must be sent. That is why we send brothers out, only brothers with a good name: “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” The glad tidings are that you are the Israelites, Christ died for you and your race, and he is coming back to save our race.

thread.label: Romans 12:2
thread.text: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: Psalms 119:9
precepts.why:
Paul says, “be not conformed to this world”, because of who rules over this world: the white man. Don't have the mind of the Edomite, the mind of Cain. Instead, “be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”, after Christ. Just before, Ephesians told us, “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” That is what we have to do. But how do we really go about doing it?

David asks the same question: “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way?” How can we cleanse our ways? “by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

The renewing of the mind comes by the word. We have to take heed according to the word, and that is how the bitter spirit, the leaven of Cain and Esau, is cleansed out, so that we may prove “what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:1-2
precepts.why:
Peter shows what the renewing of the mind looks like: “Wherefore laying aside all malice.” Lay aside all malice, family: all malice, all leaven. “and all guile”: that is the fake talk, because you are bitter. “and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings.” We have to lay these things aside.

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” We have to be born again in Christ like newborn babes. The sincere milk of the word is the thing we have to desire, and it is what makes us grow.

This is Romans 12:2 at work. Being conformed to this world is carrying the mind of Cain and Esau: the malice, the guile, the envy and the evil speaking of the bitter spirit. Being transformed is laying all of that aside and feeding on the word until the mind is renewed after Christ.

precepts.label: James 1:21-24
precepts.why:
James tells us what to put off and what to take in: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The word received with meekness is what saves the soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” We have to be doers of the word, family. We hear the class about putting away all bitterness, and then we don't do it.

“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” When you read the scriptures, you see yourself in them. But after you read them, you go your way and don't really address the matter.

We don't want to do that. We want to examine ourselves, look to the scriptures and say: Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit. I'm bitter toward my wife, I'm bitter toward the leadership, I'm bitter toward my brother. We have to confess that thing and pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is being transformed by the renewing of the mind, and not conformed to this world.

thread.label: 1 Corinthians 2:7
thread.text: But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory:

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 13:2
precepts.why:
“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom”. Paul was one who understood that mystery. He wrote: “And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains”.

Prophecy is a gift, and Paul had the gift of prophecy. He understood all mysteries. That is why, when we read the book of Hebrews, we understand a lot of things in Genesis: because of the letters of Paul. Paul explained a lot of things and took them to another level, making them plain for us, even things in the law that we do not fully understand.

He had all knowledge and all faith. So when Paul says “we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery”, he is speaking as a man who was given to understand the mysteries, the hidden wisdom which God ordained before the world unto our glory. That hidden wisdom goes into Christ: who he was and who he is was hid from our people for all ages, and even the princes of this world did not know it, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.”

precepts.label: Matthew 13:11
precepts.why:
Christ said: “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” It is given to the apostles and certain men to understand the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; it is not given to everyone. Once these men understand it, God having revealed it to them, they reveal it to the people and the people understand it. It is given to the apostles first and foremost.

That is the wisdom of God in a mystery, the hidden wisdom. There is hidden wisdom even about Adam: did Adam have a kingdom? People think he was running around butt naked. No; it is hidden wisdom.

“but to them it is not given”. That is why there is no need to argue with anybody about what the scriptures mean. Correct them and keep it moving. If God did not open your eyes, you are not going to get it. As Paul says, “the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.” So why try to force him to know it? Correct them and dust off your shoes, because everyone is not going to get the things of the Spirit of God.

precepts.label: John 14:15
precepts.why:
“Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit”. Who are those that love him? Christ said: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

There are two types of people in this world: people who say they love God, like the Christians who all say they love the Lord and love Jesus, and people who do what Jesus said. Which one is justified? If you are not doing what he said and you say you love him, you are a liar.

To the ones who keep his commandments he sends the Spirit: “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”. And: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance”. That is how we learn the different levels of understanding in the scriptures; it starts with the apostles, and they teach the people.

So we do not teach with man's wisdom from a theology school or seminary; we teach “which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.” The things God has prepared for us, the holy city, living forever, being with Christ even if we die keeping the commandments, are on another level. They are freely given to us of God; we just have to keep his commandments.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:21
precepts.why:
“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. What is the example that Christ left? Peter: “For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps”.

Christ suffered for us: that goes back to him being our Passover, sacrificed for us. And he left an example, so as believers in Christ we must follow his steps. Christ came to bring peace. Bitterness does not do that.

So we apply the scriptures. Purge out the old sin, the old man, that we may be a new lump, a new creature in Christ, following in the steps of Christ. “Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness”. That malice is the bitterness: a dumb thought jumps in, the seed gets planted, it gets nourished, and next thing you know you have malice, hatred toward your brother, and wickedness, because it leads to sin.

“but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth”. Meaning: I have the bitter spirit, so I have to go to my brother and talk to him in sincerity and truth. Brothers sweep under the floor mats and dump out the toaster at Passover, and there is not a grain of yeast in the house, while they carry an evil eye toward a brother or bitterness toward a wife. We are the temple of God; the leaven has to come out of the spirit.

And do not tuck it away for later, like the brother who puts the bread in the storage closet during the feast and brings it back when the season is over. Following Christ's steps means letting the bitterness go entirely.

thread.text: Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints?

precepts.label: Matthew 19:28
precepts.why:
“Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints?” The law they were going to was the scribes and Pharisees. Paul said, how dare you go to them? They do not even believe in Christ, and they do not apply the laws correctly. You are supposed to go to the saints.

“Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” That is what Psalms 2 said: “be instructed, ye judges of the earth.” And the saints are not everybody who believes on Jesus: Psalms 148 says “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. The saints are the Israelites, and the Israelites will judge this planet. We might look like knuckles right now, but give us time.

“Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” The angels we are going to judge are not Michael, Gabriel or Uriel; the angels are Israel, and we will judge each other. Christ said: “Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

That is our future: judging the twelve tribes and the whole world. So how come we do not judge the small matters amongst ourselves? “set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church”. If the leaders act like they are unable to judge, get the young men; they can. Move the officers that always have an excuse out of the way, because the young men have the fire, the zeal, the desire and the understanding to do the job. “I speak to your shame. Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you?” All these years studying and not one wise brother that can handle this work? Then get the young ones.

thread.text: Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:4-9
precepts.why:
“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. That baptism is Moses teaching us the laws of God, and teaching us the gospel, teaching us about Christ, because Moses spoke with Christ. Christ said, “Before Abraham was, I am”: it was Christ that spoke directly to Moses. We often think the gospel only begins in the book of Matthew. It does not.

Ezra shows it: “And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season”. That mount is Sinai, and the long season is the forty days and forty nights. “And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”.

Moses was shown the beginning, the middle and the end of times; that is how he was able to write about it in the first five books. He even saw himself not entering the promised land. “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

“That thou lay up in thy heart the signs that I have shewed, and the dreams that thou hast seen, and the interpretations which thou hast heard: For thou shalt be taken away from all, and from henceforth thou shalt remain with my Son, and with such as be like thee, until the times be ended.”

So when Paul says our fathers “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ”, it is plain: the Israelites in the wilderness were taught the gospel through Moses, who had been with Christ on the mount. Those things are written “for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come”; we learn from our forefathers the same way the congregations scattered in Asia Minor did, and the acts of the apostles continue.

precepts.label: Proverbs 22:24-25
precepts.why:
“evil communications corrupt good manners.” Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes things rise, and that is what bitterness does. The root of bitterness corrupts your spirit and messes with your attitude, and that angry influence spreads to others through words and through attitude.

So Proverbs warns: “Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go”. You see that brother is bitter; he is like that dangerous overgrown brush. There could be a viper in there, anything on the other side of that bush. Move.

“Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.” Now that bitter brother has put the bitter spirit on you. You got bit, like Bird Box, and now you are looking dumb. That is the snare right there.

That is why the scripture says be not deceived. Keeping company with the bitter brother is how the leaven gets into you. His evil communications will corrupt your good manners, and his offenses will reach others, starting with the first offense, the one in your own house.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 7:10
thread.text: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:28-31
precepts.why:
Paul says “the sorrow of the world worketh death.” Here is what that worldly sorrow looks like: “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me”. When the Lord increases the affliction, after you have been wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord: it's getting real down here, the persecution is on, I ain't got no food. You call, and the line says the number you have dialed is no longer available to you, dummy. You'll seek him early, like getting on a pre-call, and you still won't find him. You won't have any connection to the Lord on that day.

Why? “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. They had the carnal mind, the mind of Cain and Esau, and cast the word behind their back like their father did. “They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.” They literally threw the word behind their back, and a lot of our brothers and sisters do that. We all have to examine ourselves.

“Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.” If you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap.

That is Esau's sorrow. He sold his birthright, then realized, damn, I want that blessing back, and cried bitterly over what he himself threw away. So we have to be sincere when we come to the Lord and have the real godly sorrow that works repentance to salvation, to our inheritance, not to be repented of. We can't be out here faking the funk.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 12:2
thread.text: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 9:7
precepts.why:
Paul explains the heavens: “I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.” Verse 4 names it: “How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” You have the sky, then space, and then where the Lord dwells, paradise, the third heaven. Those unspeakable words likely go into the name, which it is not lawful to speak.

So when Genesis says God created the heaven, it is a similitude. It is not only the sky down here; he also created paradise. Wisdom of Solomon 9 shows it was made in the beginning. Solomon says, “Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters: Thou hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein thou dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning.” When was it prepared? From the beginning, which is Genesis: when God made the firmament and called it heaven. That is not only the firmament down here; it is paradise, the third heaven.

“And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments.” That is Christ; he was there. Then Solomon prays, “O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee.” That is how you know what pleases God: wisdom has to come and show you.

Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of what is in the heavens, and that is why the temple's pattern, which Ezekiel describes next, tells us how the heavens are built.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 41:16
precepts.why:
Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of the holy tabernacle in heaven, so the temple's layout tells us about the heavens. Ezekiel 41:16: “The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories”. Three stories, three floors. Read on and it tells you there are chambers, a chamber here and a chamber there, the way 2 Esdras speaks of the chambers of souls.

It is no coincidence that the temple was built with three stories. It goes into the same thing Paul mentioned: the third heaven, where paradise is. The levels of the temple match the levels of the heavens: the sky of this earth, then space, then paradise. And above them all is the Father, at the very top, like the holy of holies.

So the three stories of Ezekiel's temple help explain “caught up to the third heaven.” Paul was taken up to the top story God built, paradise, which was made in the beginning when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

precepts.label: Genesis 6:16
precepts.why:
Noah's ark was built the same way. “A window shalt thou make to the ark”: there is that window again, like the narrow windows of the temple. “and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof”: the door is in the side of the boat. “with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.” A lower level, a second level and a third.

The ark had three levels, the same as the temple. It is basically a floating temple. God gave Noah the same pattern he gave Solomon, and both follow the way the heavens are built.

Temple, ark and heavens all show the same three stories, and that is how Paul could speak of being caught up to the third heaven. Paradise is the third story, and the Father dwells above all of it.

precepts.label: Amos 9:6
precepts.why:
“It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven”. What are the stories he builds in the heaven? The first layer, the second layer and the third layer: the sky of this earth, space, and paradise. Paul calls it the third heaven. Those are the stories, three different layers.

Above them is the Father, at the very top, the holy of holies. Where he is, is infinite; it is called eternity. That is why we call him the Majesty on high. He is the highest, and the Most High, the Highest, is one of the few titles Christ does not have. That title is his Father's. They are not the same person.

Read on: “and hath founded his troop in the earth”. The troop is us. “he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name.” From there, back to Genesis 1:6: “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters”. The waters are space, and the firmament was made in the midst of space. Atmosphere means vapor sphere, and vapor means water: layers of water that circle the earth and protect it from the sun. So there are levels of heaven over the earth, then space, then paradise, with levels there too. As above, so below. Paradise was created on the second day, when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

thread.text: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?

classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: Proverbs 14:10
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves”: not your neighbor, yourself. And you can do it, because “The heart knoweth his own bitterness”. Your mind knows its own bitterness. Brother, sister, you can't play confused when somebody asks, man, where is that bitterness coming from?

“and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.” So you can't say, oh Bishop, tell me what's going on with me. You know exactly what is going on in your mind. Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is. We can say, brother, you're off, you ain't moving right, there is sin in there; we may not know it specifically, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with.

This is a heavy topic. A lot of brothers and sisters are bitter. It came up in our congregation with a brother dealing with his wife, and then we came down here and saw the same thing, and it destroyed a household. If that spirit is left unchecked it can destroy the congregation. That is why each of us has to prove our own self: the heart already knows where the bitterness is.

precepts.label: Psalms 139:23-24
precepts.why:
To examine ourselves we ask the Lord to do it with us: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me”. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly.

How is he going to do that? When you say, Lord, search me, that means you have to search the scriptures. The Lord ain't going to come down and say, open that door right there, let me see what's behind it. No, brother. You have to search the scriptures.

Then, in order to get over the root of bitterness, we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. We look to the scriptures and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit, bitter toward my wife, toward the leadership, toward my brother, and we pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is how we prove our own selves, whether we be in the faith.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 1:22
precepts.why:
James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.” The heathen are the northern kingdom. Peter already knew this. God had shown him that he could not call any man common or unclean. He sat with them, and he convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right, that God had granted them repentance unto life too.

“But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.” When certain came from James, Peter “withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.” Dissimulation means deception, hypocrisy, pretence, deceit, fakery: in other words, being fake. Paul said to him before them all, you are being fake like they were fake. Peter knew better, and he was corrected in front of everybody. He would have been embarrassed and ashamed.

But he repented. And as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake. So Peter wrote “Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently”.

Peter came back and taught it after he learned it: I was wrong. We cannot have fake love for the brethren, because God already showed me, and when I was put to the test I was influenced not to accept them. So the message now is, do not have feigned love for the brethren.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:13
precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man.” Bitterness is a very common thing that many of us battle with. We are never alone in it: if leadership sees a spirit in one congregation, they have to understand that the same spirit is elsewhere. That is the “one body, and one Spirit” of Ephesians 4:4. The classes are not rehearsed, yet the same talking points come out in different places, because the Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to address the prevalent issue of the time, and in the midst of Passover He revealed bitterness throughout the congregations.

“But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” Even while being tried and tempted, the Lord in His faithfulness makes a way out.

What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother. Speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind, and we create a whole other reality that does not even exist in real life. You talk to the brother and you say, damn, all that mess I was thinking and rehearsing is not even the case.

That matters, because bitterness is the hidden leaven that must be purged. If it is not purged, it grows into a root that defiles the soul. Many brothers who left the body and came out with crazy videos started with a root of bitterness.

thread.text: And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers;

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 14:1
precepts.why:
“And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”. The Lord made some of us inside here apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers, and some brothers have several of these gifts. Why did God put his Holy Spirit in us and give us these gifts? Not so you can exalt yourself: I'm the mighty deacon, I understand all these things. It is “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry”. The gift is not for your own selfish reasons. It is to make the brothers better and the people perfect, and to help your people. You brothers travelling the world teaching the gospel are waking people up all over the world.

So Paul says “Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.” Desire spiritual gifts, but rather prophesy. Why? “But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.”

When you prophesy you teach and edify the people. You exhort the brothers to continue in the faith and to have hope; that is how brothers develop hope and faith, when the prophets among us go into the scriptures and show certain things. That feeling inside when you hear brothers teach who can prophesy is exhortation, and it revives you.

And it comforts, because we need that comfort. We are all going through certain things, and we are all tired of this world and this life. But when we go into the scriptures and see the things the Lord has prepared for us, it comforts us and exhorts us to continue in this gospel and this work. That is why the gifts are for the body and not for oneself.

precepts.label: Ephesians 3:17
precepts.why:
The gifts are given “For the perfecting of the saints”, and prophecy gives edification, exhortation and comfort. Paul prays for the same: “That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge”.

With all the saints you have to comprehend the breadth, the width, the length, the depth and the height. It goes into what the Lord has prepared for those of us that love him. Once you fully understand that, it gives you hope, exhorts you and comforts you to continue in this walk and not fall out and go back into the world.

Some brothers and sisters have been with us for years and say, I can't take it no more, five years and I ain't got none, and they go back into the world and let Satan overcome them. If you want a husband or a wife, go to the Lord first: pray and fast, Lord, send me a righteous sister, send me a righteous husband. But get yourself right first, or it is not coming your way. Sisters want an Abraham but are not like Sarah; brothers want a Sarah while still living with mama.

“that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God. Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us, Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end.” That world without end is the church, a precept with Isaiah 45. Rooted and grounded in love, we comprehend what the Lord has for us and are filled with his fulness.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:12-13
precepts.why:
Ephesians 4 says what to put away: “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” Bitterness comes first, and the rest come along with it: wrath, anger, clamour, and evil speaking, talking foolish and reckless about the brother, the sister, your wife. That thing has to be put away with extreme hatred. Instead: “be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.” You want to seek pardon from the Lord, but you have hatred toward your brother?

Colossians says what to put on in its place: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” That is how we have to move. The elect of God forbear and forgive one another.

Offenses are going to come in the congregation: a brother says something, a sister says something, and somebody gets offended. We all have to have mercy on one another, because we are all sick. This is a hospital. If a brother coughs on you, you forgive the brother, because everybody in here is sick.

This is how the bitter leaven gets purged. It came up in one congregation where a brother was bitter with his wife and it destroyed a household, and the same spirit showed up elsewhere. Left unchecked, it can destroy a congregation, so we put off the bitterness and put on mercy and forgiveness, as Christ forgave us.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:22
precepts.why:
“Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh”. These are the same scriptures Esau uses to justify slavery, and that dumb black people use to reject the Bible. But it is not talking about chattel slavery. It is what was read in Leviticus 25 and Exodus: Israel, in a time of stability, still following the laws on selling yourself to work if you were poor or owed debts.

Leviticus says it: “And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile”. Then he departs, he and his children, back to his own family, because “Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour”. Rigour is chattel slavery, and God forbade it over a brother.

Colossians says the same: “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. The servants were Israelites, Hebrew servants, hired servants.

Exodus 21 shows the master: “If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.” If his master gave him a wife and she bore children, he could say, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free”. Why would he say, I love my master? Because the brother treated him real good. That is what “Servants, obey in all things your masters” is talking about.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:18
precepts.why:
“Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.” This is in the slave Bible; Esau used it. But the good and gentle masters and the froward ones were Israelite masters. The law said not to deal with Israel with rigour, meaning hard, yet some of them were like that. The froward ones are the ones who did not really like you.

“For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.”

Why would a master not like his servant? Exodus 22: a thief found breaking in, “If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.” That is different from a poor brother saying, I lack food, clothing and shelter, will you help me? If I broke into your house, stole all your stuff and got caught, now I have to work for you, and you are not going to like me too much. You have to see him every morning.

So Peter tells servants to be subject even to the froward master, and to take it patiently. It is Israelite servitude under the law, not chattel slavery.

precepts.label: Titus 2:9
precepts.why:
“Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again”: not talking back. Esau perverted this. But read on: “Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.” To purloin is to steal something: sticky fingers, a kleptomaniac. That is what was read in Exodus 22. Paul is dealing with brothers who were stealing, got caught, and were sold to make restitution.

Philemon shows it plainly. Paul met Onesimus while under arrest. He had been a servant to Philemon, and he ran away: “For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever; Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved”. Deal with him like a brother beloved.

Was he a servant because he was poor, or because he did something bad? “If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account”. He owed something because he stole or broke something, and Paul said, put it on my account.

So Paul was dealing with servants who were Hebrews, Israelites in servitude to other Israelites. Chattel slavery came later, when Israel fell by the edge of the sword and was led away captive into all nations, under Rome, Spain and Portugal, France, Britain and the United States.

precepts.label: Galatians 1:6
precepts.why:
How did “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters” become a scripture used to justify chattel slavery? This is what they did: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.”

That is what Esau did. They took this Bible and perverted it. The servants of Ephesians, Colossians, Peter and Titus were Israelites serving Israelites under the law, hired servants and sojourners who went free in the seventh year and at the jubilee, and whom God said not to rule with rigour. Esau took those scriptures and made them into the slave Bible, to justify ruling over us with rigour in chattel slavery.

And dumb black people, seeing how Esau used them, reject the Bible altogether, not knowing it was perverted.

But God says, “Fear not: for I have redeemed thee”. He gave Egypt for our ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for us, because we are precious in his sight, and he will give men for us. He will bring our seed from the east and gather us from the west, say to the north, give up, and deliver us into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is the true jubilee.

precepts.label: Amos 3:7
precepts.why:
Colossians says Christ is “the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things.” He was the first thing created, before the earth, before the heavens, before the angels. God created him and told him to create everything else: the angels, stars, planets, galaxies and paradise in heaven, and a spiritual realm that cannot be seen.

Moses saw the secrets of that time, creation included, and wrote about it in a similitude, and a lot of it he hid. Those hidden things are the secrets of wisdom, and they are double: a scripture says one thing and also another thing, and when we read it again the Most High takes us to see it on another level.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The secrets Moses hid, God reveals to His servants the prophets. Paul and the apostles understood the depth and width of the knowledge of God, because the spirit of God revealed the hidden mysteries to them. After the last of the apostles’ students died, that understanding died with them and all kinds of paganism came into the church.

But God has sent His sons back on the earth, and the proper understanding of these scriptures is coming back out. People question it when they hear that the men of IUIC are prophets. We are going to show you the secrets, and you judge for yourself.

precepts.label: Titus 1:14
precepts.why:
“And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.” That is why people have left the truth of the word of God to follow fables. Christmas is a fable. All of those are fables, meaning lies, story-told lies, with symbolic meanings in the stories: Santa Claus and his blackened helper, Santa with his horse in the Netherlands and his flying reindeer here, Rudolph and the fairy dust. Our people have celebrated this foolishness for a long time.

Titus gives the warning: “Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.” Don’t give heed to them. Christmas and all these things are commandments of men, and they turn you from the truth.

That is why you have people online saying it is not wrong to celebrate Christmas, it is in your heart, it is how you feel, and all that crap. It is turning you from the truth of God. Some try to figure it out: we agree his birthday is not December 25th, so we can make up another day. That is what they do, but it always comes back to December 25th. It is still a fable and a commandment of men, and Paul told Timothy the people would turn away their ears from the truth to follow it.

precepts.label: John 10:22
precepts.why:
There is a winter holiday that Christ kept: “And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.” Read on: “And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.” The feast of dedication is celebrated in the winter, and Christ was there at the feast in the wintertime.

So the holiday of the winter that Christ kept was the feast of dedication, not a December birthday. Christmas, December 25th and the birthday of Christ are fables and commandments of men, and people have turned their ears from the truth to follow them.

The same goes for the new year. The new year is in the spring, not the winter. Abib, or Aviv, means spring: the season when the young, tender barley ears first appear, marking the start of the religious new year around March or April in the Gregorian calendar, the time of the Passover and the firstfruits offering, signifying renewal and freedom from Egypt. They celebrate the new year in the winter. And if you see Israelite groups keeping Passover in February, or July, or June, there is something wrong. The truth is in the scriptures; the winter birthday and the winter new year are the fables they turned to.

precepts.label: Song of Solomon 8:5
precepts.why:
“Not giving heed to Jewish fables.” A fable is a lie, and it says Jewish because it pertains to the Jews. Christ was a Jew, and there is a lie being told that he was born on December 25th. That is a Jewish fable. Christmas goes back into slavery and into paganism too, and it turns you away from the truth of serving God. It has nothing to do with Christ.

Luke tells what happened: “the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger.” Her firstborn, meaning she had many sons; the Catholic Church says Mary was a virgin who never had sex, but she brought forth her firstborn. And before he was put in the manger, the prophecy in the Song of Solomon shows where he was born: “Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth.”

So Mary had Christ under an apple tree, and after she gave birth to him there, she took him to the manger, “because there was no room for them in the inn.” Christ was not born in the manger. A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime they are not out there; they go in the barn to stay warm.

Why was there no room in the inn, the hotel? “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.” Everybody came up to Jerusalem at that time and the inns were full, because it was the Passover. Christ was born in the springtime, not in the winter.

That is how the scripture kills the fable. Stop listening to Santa Claus, aka Pope Nicholas, St. Nicholas. Don’t give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you from the truth: Christ was not born on December 25th.

thread.text: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 8:52
precepts.why:
“For we which have believed do enter into rest.” What is that rest that is promised? Ezra shows it: “For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom.”

This paradise is spoken to the Israelites. It is not talking about all nations. Paradise opened, the tree of life planted, a city builded and rest allowed: that is what is left to us, the promise “of entering into his rest.”

“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them.” The gospel did not begin in the book of Matthew; Christ was taught to our forefathers too. But “the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” They disobeyed Christ and were moved with unbelief, and their unbelief is what kept them from entering in. “Let us therefore fear”, then, lest any of us come short of the paradise and the rest that is allowed to Israel.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 3:5-6
precepts.why:
Paul says God’s works “were finished from the foundation of the world.” The rest is not something new; it was prepared before anything else was. Ezra shows it: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.”

Paradise was here before the earth came forth. Before Christ said the evening and the morning were the first day, paradise was already here. That is the paradise opened to Israel in 2 Esdras 8:52, where the tree of life is planted and rest is allowed.

So when Hebrews says the works were finished from the foundation of the world, it is telling you the rest was already created and waiting. Then “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” That number seven keeps coming back: the seventh day Sabbath points to that rest God prepared from the beginning.

precepts.label: Micah 4:10
precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Paul is making a comparison between our works and God’s. God worked, then rested; so must we. Micah shows the labour: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city.”

No matter what we are going through, brothers and sisters, we have to be in pain and do this work. Be in pain to bring forth the kingdom of heaven on earth.

That is why Paul says “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” Labour, labour in pain, bring forth your works to enter into that rest, which is the kingdom. Rest is entered by labour. The generation in the wilderness fell because of unbelief; the daughter of Zion must travail to bring forth.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:13
precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Revelation shows who rests and why: “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.”

They rest from their labours, and their works follow them. Your works are what are going to allow you to enter in through those gates. The rest is not handed to the idle; it comes after the labour, and the labour goes with you into it.

So “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief” that we read of in the wilderness. Labour in pain, bring forth your works, like the daughter of Zion in travail, and then rest from those labours in the kingdom.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:1-3
precepts.why:
The seventh day Sabbath, resting from our servile work, is a similitude the Most High uses for us resting in the kingdom when it is established. That is the true rest, when we will really rest from servile work. Because after the Sabbath some of us have to go to work on Sunday, then Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, slaving for Esau.

Isaiah shows the day of that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.” The nations are going to be joined with us, but how? “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” They are our possession.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” That is the true rest: rest from our sorrow, from our fear, and from the hard bondage we were made to serve.

That is why “if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.” That Jesus is Joshua. Joshua was mighty and smote the Hamites, but we did not get true rest in the land; there were enemies on all sides, the Amalekites and the Hamites we were fighting. The true rest is the kingdom of God on earth, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.”

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:7-8
precepts.why:
“And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” Peter shows how that seventh day reaches forward to the kingdom: “But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men. But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.”

One day with the Lord, brothers, is a thousand years. So the seventh day is not only the Sabbath we keep each week; it maps to a thousand years, the reign that comes after the heavens and earth that are now are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment.

That is why “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” The rest of the seventh day is the similitude, and the thousand years is the substance: the day we reign with Christ, as Revelation 20:4 shows.

precepts.label: Revelation 20:4
precepts.why:
If one day with the Lord is a thousand years, what is the seventh day rest? Revelation shows it: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

They lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. That is going into the rest. The seventh day Sabbath represents us resting with Christ, and every seventh day is rehearsing it.

The rest promised in Hebrews is not the land Joshua brought us into, and not only the one day a week before going back to labour in Esau’s system. It is the eternal reign with Christ when he comes back, sitting on thrones with judgment given to us, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Seven represents completion, and the seventh day points to that completion: the kingdom and the thousand years with Christ.

thread.text: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Matthew 6:10
precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” We want God's kingdom to be in earth as it is in heaven, and that is what we are praying for right now: the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

This ties to the rest of Hebrews 4. When Genesis says God “rested on the seventh day from all his work”, it does not mean God was tired and went to get some sleep. Moses is an analogy, a similitude. Hebrews says “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day”: God's rest is a place, paradise. 2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was planted before the earth, and leading Adam into paradise is entering into his rest.

That is the kingdom of Adam. When Adam had dominion on the earth, it was on a much higher level than people think. Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth, the only flesh, him and his wife, that could, until he committed sin; flesh and blood cannot be up there because of that sinful nature. How Adam was on the earth is basically how we are going to be in the future, the difference being that he was not in the flesh as we are. So when we pray “Thy kingdom come”, we are praying for what was once on the earth in Adam's day to be on the earth again.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 11:21
precepts.why:
“That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” What does Moses mean? When you go into the land and keep the commandments, it will be as the days of heaven upon the earth.

Moses saw Adam's kingdom. That is why he could say that going into the land and keeping the laws would be as the kingdom of heaven upon the earth. The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam was ruling.

So the promise of Hebrews 4:1, “a promise being left us of entering into his rest”, is the same promise: heaven's days upon the earth again. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Those to whom the word was first preached “entered not in because of unbelief”, “For we which have believed do enter into rest”. The one who has entered into his rest has “ceased from his own works”: the works are our labouring in this earth to bring forth the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:2
precepts.why:
“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” Remember, it withdrew itself; now it is coming back.

2 Esdras 7:26 says it: “the bride shall appear, and she coming forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth.” That bride withdrawn from the earth is the holy city Jerusalem, the access to the spirit realm, which withdrew itself from the earth. For it to be withdrawn from the earth it must once have been on the earth, and it was, during the time of Adam. Adam was not running around butt naked; Adam was going back and forth to a spiritual realm.

The city is described with twelve gates for the twelve tribes of Israel and no heathens. So the tribes were around back then, and Adam went through a gate, the Judah gate. The twelve tribes around in the beginning were called the sons of God; Moses did not name them because the Lord said to hide these things. Jacob, Esau, will never go through those gates. They may stand outside and look at it and drop some stuff off in front of it, but they will never enter into those gates.

The city was prepared from the foundation of the world; it is already built, from the beginning. It is the rest God entered, the paradise Adam was led into, and the promise of Hebrews 4:1 that we must not come short of.

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:10
precepts.why:
Rome taught that in order to be saved you must be water baptized. Hebrews 6 answers it: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection”. The principles of the doctrine of Christ are animal sacrifice. The principle goes to the beginning; that is how we got forgiveness of sin at first. And among the things we must leave, Paul names “the doctrine of baptisms”.

Hebrews 9:10 shows what those washings were: “Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation”. Divers washings are carnal ordinances. They were imposed only until the time of reformation, and then they were to end.

So when Hebrews 6:1 says leave the principles, it means leave the meats, the drinks and the divers washings with the animal sacrifices. We did not get perfection in animal sacrifice, and water baptism belongs with those carnal ordinances.

precepts.label: Exodus 30:19
precepts.why:
Where did the washing come from? Exodus 30:19: “For Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet thereat”. The priests washed at the laver. This is where John the Baptist got it from.

Isaiah shows what the washing symbolized: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil”. The water was a symbol of putting away evil.

John the Baptist did not make up water baptism. It came from the priests, and John was in the lineage of the priesthood; he was a Levite. So the doctrine of baptisms that Hebrews 6 says to leave is the priests' washing, one of the old ordinances Christ, the new high priest, brought to an end.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 2:22
precepts.why:
Jeremiah shows that the water never took away sin: “For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God”. Wash all you want with nitre and much soap; the iniquity is still marked before God.

That is the proof that the washing was always symbolic. It came from the priests, from Aaron and his sons washing at the laver, and it was a sign of cleansing, not the cleansing itself.

So go back to Hebrews 6:1 and stress the word leaving: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection”. Leave the animal sacrifice, and leave the doctrine of baptisms with it. Rome's teaching that you must be dumped in the water to be saved is going back to what Paul said to leave.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:11
precepts.why:
The doctrine of baptisms Hebrews 6 says to leave includes John the Baptist. John said it himself: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”.

John used water. Christ baptizes with the Holy Ghost and with fire, not using water. Christ never used water, because water baptism was to end. It was always symbolic.

So when Paul says “let us go on unto perfection”, the baptism we go on to is Christ's, with the Holy Ghost and fire. The water was part of the principles we leave behind.

precepts.label: Leviticus 16:21
precepts.why:
Hebrews 6:2 goes on to “laying on of hands”, and Leviticus shows where that came from: “And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat”. That is what we did. The high priest laid his hands on the goat to put the sins of Israel upon it.

So Paul was saying: all that stuff the priests were doing, we have to leave it. Christ is the new high priest. The laying on of hands belongs with the animal sacrifice and the washings, the principles we leave to go on unto perfection.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 12:43
precepts.why:
Hebrews 6:2 also names “resurrection of the dead”, and 2 Maccabees shows how that was handled under the old ordinances: “And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing therein very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection”. A sin offering sent to Jerusalem for the dead. That is how we thought we got the resurrection, through the sacrifice.

So Paul lists them all to leave: “the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. And this will we do, if God permit”. In Paul's letters they were still doing those things. It finally came to an end, with no ifs, ands or buts, in 70 AD, when Esau destroyed the temple, put the priests in slavery, and many of us fled into Africa. It was finished.

And there is no going back: “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”, “If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame”. Some Israelites said we have got to go back to animal sacrifice and water baptism. If you leave Christ and go back to that stuff, you cannot be renewed. They never believed. Brothers and sisters who leave this truth and go back to white Jesus and water baptism, we can't help them.

precepts.label: Exodus 5:14
precepts.why:
Moses “refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God”. Understand that in ancient Egypt everybody was not bad off. Things were not bad for Moses; Moses made things bad for himself by killing the Egyptian, and there was a consequence for killing an Egyptian, so Moses was on the run.

Exodus 5:14 shows that some of our own people were set up over us: “And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick both yesterday and to day, as heretofore?” The taskmasters set officers of the children of Israel over us. In ancient Egypt they were called officers; in America they are called Uncle Tom Negroes, house Negroes.

To be an officer you were making money. Some of our people in ancient Egypt had money and high standing, a form of good living, and they were okay with the oppression they were going through, until the officers started getting their behinds whooped too.

It is the same thing today: Beyoncé, Usher, the pastor praying for Trump, people with money who are comfortable here in modern day Egypt, spiritual Egypt. When a people live in oppression for centuries, oppression becomes a norm and you take it as a way of life. That is why the scripture talks about us trusting in the shadow of Egypt, trusting in oppression. Moses had that comfort and refused it, choosing to suffer affliction with the people of God.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:8-10
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns of the “root of bitterness springing up”, and John shows what spirit jumps on you when you move that way. “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” That is the history being drawn out from Cain to Esau: the devil sinned from the beginning, and the same spirit runs down through his children.

“For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.” The purpose of Christ is to destroy the works of the devil. So why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think that we are moving in the spirit of Christ?

“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God.” This is the manifestation of the children of God. If you don't do righteousness, you are not of God. The scripture tells us how to deal uprightly with our brother and sister: if there is an offense, go by Matthew 18:15. You don't sow discord and murmur in the midst of the congregation and spread that spirit through our brothers and sisters.

“neither he that loveth not his brother.” When you don't love your brother, you are not moving in the spirit of Christ and you are not counted a child of God. You are the son and daughter of Cain, of Esau. We have to be mindful of this spirit and purge that leaven, that bitter spirit, out of us.

precepts.label: Romans 8:6-7
precepts.why:
Esau was a man of the field and a profane person: his religion is sin. Paul gives the name for that mind: “For to be carnally minded is death.” To be carnally minded is to be Edomite minded, the profane mind. It is death, and that is why he is called the son of perdition.

“but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” When you are spiritually minded, you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean we always have to be buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers turn a brother into an enemy like a rival team in sports, stay pumped up against him and hold on to that feeling, waiting to get back at him. That is the carnal mind. Stay in the spirit.

“Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God.” The Edomite mind, the mind of the spirit of Cain, goes against God and is not subject to his law.

So there are the children of God and the children of the devil, with no in between: either the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The bitter spirit that holds a grudge against a brother is the carnal mind of Esau, and it leads to the same death and rejection he found.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:16-17
precepts.why:
This is the Edomite mindset, the carnal mind at war with God. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Unto the wicked, the white man, God says: hold on, you are carnally minded. Why are you out there talking about in God we trust? Why are you swearing in on the Bible when you do nothing according to the scriptures?

“Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” He talks about in God we trust while he has transgenders out there, putting two men together. They don't do anything the scriptures say. They cast the word behind their back, because the carnal mind is at war with God.

This is the battle of the spirit and the flesh, and that inner battle is within us too. It is the same profane spirit Hebrews names in Esau, whose religion is sin and who despised what was sacred. So we have to make sure we stand in the spirit, and not take God's covenant in our mouth while we cast his words behind us, as a brother does when he holds on to a bitter spirit.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:28
precepts.why:
“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin.” Where is lust conceived? In your mind; that is where the root begins. Christ shows exactly how: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” That is how lust is conceived.

We are living in an evil world, and we all see beautiful women. A picture of an immodestly dressed woman was put on the screen and the brothers were asked one by one what they saw. One liked the way she dressed. Another said she is beautiful, but the way she dresses you have to hate that thing, she has to be modest. Another said, I have been in the world a lot longer than in the truth, so I am working on hating it. What you see on the screen you see every damn day when you go outside, and some of you break your neck walking down the street.

You have to train yourself to hate evil. It doesn’t come naturally; you cannot come to the truth and all of a sudden hate what you see out there. When you see her, train your mind: she has AIDS, she stinks, she has to be a man. If you don’t, you will always be watching and desiring these things. Older brothers with experience have matured past it; the young brothers dealing with youthful lusts have to train. Sisters, before the truth many of you walked around in miniskirts and spandex, giggling and giving out your number to every dude on the block, and now you have changed how you dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up.

So you see it, and in your mind you say, damn, I don’t mind sleeping with that. When you allow that thought, lust is conceived, and sin comes forth. But if the thought comes and you shake it off, what’s wrong with you, God is going to kill you, stop thinking like that, it is not conceived. If you sit down and entertain it, it brings forth sin. That is why Christ says adultery doesn’t start when you literally lie down with a woman; it starts in your mind. “and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Some say I fornicated and I didn’t die; that death is damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you.
