precepts.label: 1 Peter 1:1
precepts.why:
Peter writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”, and verse 2 calls them “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ”. These strangers are the same strangers that came to keep the Passover in Chronicles, and the elect is the same name given to those called according to Hosea and Isaiah in Romans 9. Who's that? Israel.

So when verse 9 says “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”, the “ye” is these same strangers scattered abroad. They are set against “them which be disobedient”: the builders that disallowed the stone, the southern kingdom, the Pharisees that rejected Christ and stumbled at that stone of stumbling and rock of offence of Isaiah 8:14. They were “appointed” to it. They had to put Christ to death, and his death gave the other kingdom the chance to repent and come back into the fold. By rejecting Christ they brought back in the same brothers they rejected.

The scattered elect were called “out of darkness into his marvellous light”, which is Isaiah 9:1. And they are the ones “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” That goes back to Deuteronomy 32 and Isaiah 7, not a people. The northern tribes, cast off and scattered, are now the people of God.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:36
precepts.why:
“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the way of knowledge is the Bible. The Bible does not belong to all nations on earth; it was given only to the beloved Israelites.

That is who Peter is writing to: “This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you”, to stir up their pure minds by way of remembrance, “That ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets”. The beloved of 2 Peter 3 is Israel his beloved of Baruch, the ones the way of knowledge was given to.

So when Peter warns “that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts”, he is warning the beloved about scoffers among them. Are we not seeing scoffers in these last days, like never before? Every black urban apologist is a scoffer. They don't believe the Bible. They don't believe Christ is black. They think Jesus is Caesar Borgia and the white man is coming to deliver them.

They say “Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.” Nothing has changed. But they “willingly are ignorant”, because we can take them to Deuteronomy and show them how things were prophesied and have come to pass, and it fits us perfect to a T. How are you going to say the Bible isn't a true book, when the knowledge in it was given to you?

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:2
precepts.why:
Peter asks, since this whole earth is reserved unto fire, “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”. That means we have to act right and speak right. A lot of our conversation is filth and sports. We have to train ourselves to speak the words of this book.

When we came into the school, they used to say about one of the elders: if you weren't talking about the Bible, don't talk to him; that's all he wanted to hear. Paul said the same: “For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.” He trained himself. All I want to hear is Bible. I don't want to hear Betty got a big booty. I don't want to hear how many touchdowns somebody ran or how far he hit the jump shot. I don't want to hear that crap.

That is holy conversation, and godliness is our actions, our works: the way we live must match the way we speak. The scoffers walk after their own lusts and their conversation follows their lusts. The beloved, knowing the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, train their minds and spirits to know nothing but Christ and him crucified, so that they may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21
precepts.why:
Peter says “we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.” Isaiah 60 shows what that promise is. “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: the white man will be subdued, because he is the violent man, behind every coup and every war. The land is the land of Israel, with no “wasting nor destruction within thy borders”, and “thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light”. That doesn't mean the sun and moon are done away with; they will be there, but the Israelites won't need them, because the Lord will be our light. “Thy sun shall no more go down”: our understanding shall no more go down, and our moon, our understanding, won't withdraw itself. And “the days of thy mourning shall be ended.”

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”. That is why the new earth is one wherein dwelleth righteousness: because our people shall be all righteous. Esau isn't going to be there enjoying anything. “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation”: we're going to have a whole lot of children. “I the Lord will hasten it in his time”: I'm going to speed it up.

The scoffers say all things continue as they were. But one day is with the Lord as a thousand years; he is not slack concerning his promise. So, beloved, seeing we look for such things, be diligent to be found of him in peace, without sin, and blameless.

thread.label: 2 Peter 3:15-18
thread.text: And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you;

classes.title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.label: Romans 1:7
precepts.why:
Peter says “our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”. Peter is giving kudos and respect to Paul for the wisdom that was in him, and that wisdom is Christ, the spirit of Christ. But in Paul's epistles “are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest”. So first get clear on who Paul was writing to.

“To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.” Called to be saints. Who are the saints? Psalms 148 speaks of “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The children of Israel are the saints. We are the saints.

Some Christians say Paul was writing to Israelites and other nations at the same time. No. That is not who the letter is addressed to. It is addressed to the saints at Rome. Other nations are never referred to as saints. When you twist that and teach that your oppressor can be granted the same benefits as you, that the nations receive some twisted salvation, you have been “led away with the error of the wicked” and fallen from your own stedfastness. It is a whole different gospel, and that is how the unlearned wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 2:17
precepts.why:
Get some clarity on who Paul is writing to: “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”. Paul is writing to the Jews. There is obviously northern kingdom in the congregations too, but he is writing to Judah.

Romans 7 says the same: “Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,)”. Why does he speak to them that know the law? Because he is writing to Jews, “how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth”.

So Paul is writing to Jews, to those who know the law, to the saints at Rome. Is he addressing both Jews and Gentiles in the church? Yes, but the Gentiles there are the northern kingdom, and they are all saints. He is not writing to other nations at all.

That is why Peter says the unlearned wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”. They stumble because they think Paul was writing things out of thin air to all nations, when he was writing to Israel, men who rested in the law and boasted of God. Know who the letter is addressed to and much of what is hard to be understood in Paul becomes plain.

precepts.label: Acts 26:22
precepts.why:
What was Paul's source material? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great”, leaders and students, teachers and students, “saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. Paul only taught what Moses and the prophets said.

And in Acts 28, when many came to his lodging, he “expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” His letters are based on the law and the prophets. He was not sitting around making things up.

That is why Peter mentions “the other scriptures”: to understand Paul's letters you must understand the other scriptures. Are there places where the spirit of Christ spoke through Paul and things were added? Yes. Paul's letters are 99.9 percent law and prophets, and maybe one percent is something like the unbelieving wife departing, which is not found in Moses, because under Moses, if she did not believe, she got death. Your wife could believe in Satan in the wilderness and she got death. That was added for that time, and that is “the wisdom given unto him”: Christ speaking through Paul.

When people don't study Paul, they say Paul's letters aren't authoritative, Mark and Luke weren't of the twelve, and they begin to speak evil of dignities. Then the Lord blinds their minds, and Satan has them teaching that nations can be saved. We have been thoroughbreds in Paul's letters since learning Acts 10 and Romans 11 at the Bishop's house in 2006.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 21:27
precepts.why:
John says “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Even the scribes and Pharisees took on the spirit of Cain, of Satan; they moved in the same exact spirit, bitter toward Christ and wanting to put him to death. That spirit will jump on us too, and we have to deal with it. When we are overcome with it, we take on the same attributes Cain did.

“When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” You will have brothers and sisters say, the white man is the devil, they're going to be destroyed, they're going into captivity. And meanwhile you are moving in the same spirit. So you curse Satan, and you curse your own soul, because you have hatred toward your brother. Brothers talk bold against the white man and find themselves in the same spirit as him.

“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.” Whoever is bitter toward his brother is in the spirit of Cain; you are in the same spirit. That hatred is always masked: “Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” He acted like his friend to get him in position.

So we have to exercise ourselves to have a conscience void of offence. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God. Don't allow it to fester and resonate in your spirit until you are overcome, because “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren.”

precepts.label: Baruch 3:4
precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”. The “their” is the Israelites. Why does it call us dead bodies? Baruch 3:4 answers: “O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee”.

When we sin against God, God refers to us as dead. Remember the scripture says, keep my commandments and live. So Israelites living in sin are dead Israelites, even while they are walking around.

“And not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave unto us.” That is why the plagues cleave unto us. One of those plagues is us going into slavery on ships: the transatlantic slave trade was a plague, one of the curses of Deuteronomy 28. Moses said we would go into tribulation again, this time by ships, and be sold to our enemies.

So the dead bodies lying in the street of the great city are the Israelites, spiritually dead, disconnected from our God, under the plagues that came because we did not hearken.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:10
precepts.why:
Baruch goes on: “How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land”? Now we are in our enemies’ land. America is your enemies’ land; they are the ones ruling this place.

“That thou art waxen old in a strange country”: we have waxed old in strange countries, because our land is the land of Israel.

“That thou art defiled with the dead”. What does it mean that we are defiled with the dead? We walk around like zombies. We have broken God’s laws and we are living in these lands not knowing who we are. We are confused; we call ourselves all kinds of different names and titles. We are the congregation of the dead, the valley of dry bones. That is us today.

That is why Revelation 11:8 says “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”: the twelve tribes of Israel, spiritually dead, disconnected from God, lying in the streets of our enemies’ land.

precepts.label: Revelation 17:5
precepts.why:
The dead bodies lie “in the street of the great city”. Where is that great city? Revelation 17:5: “And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.”

That great city is Mystery Babylon, and Mystery Babylon is America: the greatest city on this earth, the greatest country on this earth.

And it is the great city “which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”. The same spirit that was in Sodom and Gomorrah, the homosexuality, the lesbianism, all that filth, is the same spirit here in America. And the same spirit that was in ancient Egypt is here. Egypt means bondage, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. What happened to the Israelites in ancient Egypt, the oppression, has happened to them here in America, and is still happening. The curses of Deuteronomy 28 include the diseases of Egypt, because those curses were some of the same things that were on us in Egypt.

So the great city where the Israelites lie spiritually dead is Mystery Babylon, America, spiritual Sodom and spiritual Egypt, and this Passover points to our exodus out of her.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 7:10
precepts.why:
“And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another”. Esau rejoiced over our downfall and made merry, as in Merry Christmas. We always thought, we were the gifts, and the history shows it: when Count Frederick von Hanau acquired a large part of what is now Suriname from the Dutch West India Company, he also received as a gift an Angolan man. They sent us around as gifts. Our sons, our daughters, our mothers and fathers were the gifts, because the two prophets, the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel, tormented them; we didn't play with Esau.

The Ecclesiastes called for at this moment is Solomon's word: “I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.” See that right there. The young Black Israelites in those European paintings were supposed to be the princes over Spain and Portugal, and they became servants to the white man: children snatched from their mothers, baptized and made slaves, holding the umbrella, the mirror, tending the horses and cattle.

So when you go into museums in America, France and England and see a picture of a little Black boy holding an umbrella, don't say, oh, look at that cute little Black boy. Now you know the history as it was: those were their slaves, the Moors, the Black Jews of Spain and Portugal, separated from their parents and given a limited education so they could be dumbed down. Princes walking as servants, and nations making merry and sending them one to another as gifts.

thread.label: Revelation 13:1
thread.text: And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:18
precepts.why:
John “saw a beast rise up out of the sea”. When the Bible talks about a beast, it is talking about a race of men. Solomon says so: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” Men are beasts.

So the beast of Revelation 13 is not a monster; it is a nation of men rising up out of the peoples of the world. It has seven heads: Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, with America the eighth. Its ten horns are European nations: Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland. Upon its heads is “the name of blasphemy”, and blasphemy means wicked lies against God.

And this beast carries the attributes of the beasts of Daniel 7: like a leopard, which is Greece; with the feet of a bear, the Persian and Median empire; and the mouth of a lion, ancient Babylon. The dragon, Satan, gives it its power, its seat and great authority. That is why things in the history of the Greeks, Persia and Babylon are being fulfilled again in these last days.

precepts.label: Revelation 17:15
precepts.why:
The beast rises “up out of the sea”. What is the sea? Revelation explains it: “The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.”

So when John says, “I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea”, he is witnessing the rise of a nation of men out of the peoples of the world. The beast is a race of men, as Ecclesiastes 3:18 shows, and the sea it comes out of is the peoples, multitudes, nations and tongues.

That nation has seven heads and ten horns, the European powers: the heads Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, with America the eighth, and the ten horns the nations of Europe. One of its heads was wounded to death: Rome, in 193 AD, when Septimius Severus, Rome's first African emperor, took the throne and the Dark Ages were ushered in. The sea is the nations, and out of them rose this European beast.

precepts.why:
“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us”. Moses understood that we would be brought into spiritual Egypt, America, and he saw America being destroyed. That is what Revelation 18 shows: “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.”

What does hold mean? A hold is like a prison. After America is destroyed, America will become a prison, a cage. The demons that said, art thou come hither to torment us before the time? That torment is going to take place here in America.

Baruch 4:35: “For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time.” The she that will be inhabited by devils is America. This place is going to be the place of torment, the prison of those same devils. When America is destroyed and Christ returns, he is going to set up a lake of fire, spiritual damnation, here in America for all the wicked.

“For a great time”: that great time is the thousand years. Revelation 20 goes into it, when hell gives up the dead and everything is destroyed. So Babylon becomes the habitation of devils, burning with a fire from the Everlasting that is long to endure.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:26
precepts.why:
Ezra is shown “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”, with an entrance so narrow that only one man can go at once. That city is the kingdom of heaven, our inheritance: “Even so also is Israel's portion. Because for their sakes I made the world”. When Adam transgressed, the entrances were made narrow, full of sorrow and travail. But “the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure”. The elder world is the old world, the kingdom of Adam, where all of us were with him, ruling.

Isaiah shows the Lord bringing that back: “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

As at the first: that is the elder world, when Adam was ruling. There were judges set up then, and the twelve tribes of Israel were set up with him at that time, ruling with him. Were we in the flesh back then? No; we were immortal. As at the beginning: the beginning is Genesis.

So the Lord is not only promising good rulers again. He is promising to restore the government of the old world, the judges and counsellors we had in the beginning, and to call that city the city of righteousness. That is the city full of all good things that Ezra saw, and it is Israel's portion.

precepts.label: Sirach 36:10
precepts.why:
“Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we. Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit thou them, as from the beginning.” As from the beginning: so the tribes of Jacob were with the Lord in the beginning, in Genesis.

In Genesis the sons of God were there. When Adam fell, the sons of God were there. There was a government set up, rulership, a kingdom set up with Adam; Adam was not running around naked. There were the gates of Levi, the gates of Benjamin, the gates of Manasses: all twelve tribes in the beginning with the Lord, in their spiritual bodies. People ask what tribe Abraham was from, what tribe Isaac was from. The twelve tribes were always there. When Moses says the sons of God, that is the twelve tribes.

“O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by thy name, and upon Israel, whom thou hast named thy firstborn.” We are named God's firstborn because he created us first, before the world began. “O be merciful unto Jerusalem, thy holy city, the place of thy rest”, and “Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.”

In these last days God has raised up the prophets that have been in his name. The prophets of old are back, in the tribes of Israel, in this building.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:13
precepts.why:
The entrances of the elder world “were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” Wisdom shows what that world was like: “For God made not death: neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living. For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthful; and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of death upon the earth”.

The generations of the world were healthful: we were living forever. There was no poison of destruction in us and no kingdom of death. The kingdom of death was established after Adam fell, when Satan was given power over this earth and began ruling it, him and his children. The kingdom of death is the white man and Satan ruling the earth. Before that was the kingdom of Adam, the kingdom of heaven. That is why Moses could promise “the days of heaven upon the earth”: he saw Adam rule.

“For righteousness is immortal”: keep God's laws and you live forever. “But ungodly men with their works and words called it to them: for when they thought to have it their friend, they consumed to nought, and made a covenant with it”. A lot of our people have made a covenant with death, worshipping Satan and living in the kingdom of death. That is why the last thing Christ has to conquer is death, and then there will be no more death, period.

thread.text: And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Revelation 13:8
precepts.why:
Ezra hears the Lord say, “when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” Before the earth was made, his children were with him and they obeyed. Revelation shows that the choosing was done back then: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.”

From where? From the foundation of the world. When was your name written in the book of life? At the foundation of the world. That goes back to Genesis 1, when the Lord divided the light from the darkness and separated good from evil. That is predestination.

There is no heathen in that book. I don't care how good you think he is; they are not in the book of life. They are in the book of slavery, the register of chains. Those whose names are not written there worship the beast, because they were not chosen from the foundation of the world. And those who were written there are the ones who, in the beginning, before the world was made, did not speak against him.

precepts.label: Revelation 22:9
precepts.why:
When the world was not yet made, “no man spake against me”: everyone obeyed. We were there with the Lord in the beginning in our angelic bodies, not in this wicked fleshly body. To see what that means, look at the angel who spoke to John.

John fell down to worship before the feet of the angel, and the angel said, “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” I am a servant just like you. I am your brother. I am a prophet. And I am of them which keep the sayings of this book. That is heavy.

So now you understand a little more what the Lord means when he says that when we were with him in the beginning, we all obeyed. The angels are our brethren; we had that same celestial body with him before the earth was created, and that is why Christ says those who understand the power of God will be equal unto the angels. Now, covered in this flesh, we are rebellious, and the Lord has to keep whooping us for our idols and our evil. But you have to see who you are and believe it. This is not a fairy tale; this is real.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:1
precepts.why:
Before the world was made, everyone obeyed, because we were not in the flesh. Paul shows the body we had and will have again: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” If this body is dissolved, we have a body, not made with hands like Adam formed of the dust of the ground, but eternal in the heavens: a celestial body.

“For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”. We groan in this body because it is susceptible to sin, and we want our body from heaven. “If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.” That is what Adam's nakedness was: not running around naked, but being in the flesh. Before, he had a spiritual body; God took his spirit and put it in the flesh. That nakedness is the shame, the sinful nature.

We groan “not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.” We want our immortal body. “we walk by faith, not by sight”, “willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.”

So when you die keeping the commandments, you are present with the Lord. This is for every brother and sister who is sick, who has been told they do not have long to live, and for those who have passed away: we understand where they are. Don't be afraid. Conquer that fear. If you did what was right on this earth and dealt right with the saints, absent from this body, you will be with the Lord.

precepts.label: Proverbs 28:5
precepts.why:
Sirach says the man whose whole occupation is his worldly job shall not “understand the sentence of judgment”. Why don't you understand when judgments are passed? Proverbs answers: “Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.”

That is the brother who is always confused. When leadership makes a judgment, he doesn't agree, even if he disagrees in silence. You don't agree because you don't know the scriptures. All you know is your job, not the word of God, so you are always confused. And the Bible says you are evil.

So that brother “shall not be sought for in publick counsel”. When things are going down, we don't want to hear your opinion, because your opinion is your work, your job. He will not “sit high in the congregation” or have rank, and he will not “be found where parables are spoken”, because he could care less. If the shoe fits, brother, wear it. If you want to be a member, be a member; there is nothing wrong with that.

But they that seek the Lord understand all things. Chapter 39 shows the flip side: the one that “giveth his mind to the law of the most High”. He seeks out the wisdom of the ancients, is found where the subtle parables are, and he shall serve among great men and appear before princes.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:14
precepts.why:
Moses blesses Joseph: “Blessed of the Lord be his land, for the precious things of heaven, for the dew, and for the deep that coucheth beneath,” “And for the precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and for the precious things put forth by the moon”. Joseph's sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, dwell on islands: the Puerto Ricans and the Cubans, among others.

The precious things of heaven are the rain; the deep that coucheth beneath is the oceans that give riches beneath the waters. There are certain fruits brought forth by the sun, and certain things that come forth only by moonlight on those islands, like the coquí frog, which is nocturnal and comes out especially under the moonlight, making its noise.

That blessing points to the moon at its peak, what they call the full moon today, which is actually the new moon. That is what leads into Ecclesiasticus 43:6: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

precepts.label: Leviticus 23:1
precepts.why:
The moon serves “in her season for a declaration of times”. Leviticus 23 shows what those times are: “Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” Convocations means gatherings.

The first holy day God tells Moses to list is the Sabbath: “Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest”, instituted from Genesis 2. Then: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” He did not say seasons for the Sabbath, because the Sabbath is all year round. The ones that follow are seasonal holy days.

“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover”, in the spring. Then the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth day; Pentecost, counting fifty days; “In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets”, which is the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month; and “The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles”.

So the “declaration of times” is the high holy days. “From the moon is the sign of feasts”: every feast is counted from the new moon, when it is in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:9
precepts.why:
What is “a sign of the world”? One answer given from 2 Esdras 6:9, that Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of the world that follows, is that the sign of the world goes into our rulership and their destruction. That is not 100% wrong, and it should not be discounted.

The fuller understanding is this. The moon at its full is when we were in our full power and full understanding, in the kingdom. As it wanes and gets dark, it is us going into captivity, into full darkness. And once it gets back to fullness, it is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. That is the passing from Esau's world to Jacob's.

The moon's phases represent the stages the world is in: “a light that decreaseth in her perfection”, “increasing wonderfully in her changing”. And in the kingdom it will not wane again: “the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”, and the sun has no phases. When Jacob's world follows Esau's, there is no going back into darkness.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:1
precepts.why:
“Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise means wake up; shine means teach; and the light that is come is Christ, who said, I am the light. “For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. We are in the grossest of darkness; we have lost our heritage and lost everything. When you see the moon dark, that is what it represents: darkness has covered the whole world.

Psalms 82 shows the same darkness. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” The little g is us. Asaph, with the Holy Spirit upon him, records what we did wrong as the gods of the earth: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” We were to defend the poor and fatherless and deliver the needy, but “they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” “But ye shall die like men”: our godhood was taken from us. “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.”

Something in the heavens is out of course because of our sins. God made “two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night”. But in the kingdom, Isaiah 30:26: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases; in the kingdom the moon, the sign of the world, will not go dark again. And the sun we call so bright is not bright at all next to that.

Binding up the breach is Amos 9:11: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”, gathering the twelve tribes of Israel back again. That is when Isaiah 60:1 is fulfilled: our light is come, the moon is back at its fullness, and Israel is back in the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 5:6
precepts.why:
Under the Greeks, “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and Syria and the Philistines joined in. Others helped the Greeks, and so did one of our own.

“But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.” Jason was an Israelite, and he hated his own people. We think our people love themselves; no. He treated us like enemies, because he wanted to please the Greeks. Don't be surprised when you see black men and black women do all they can to please the enemies of our people. They will be worse on you than white men.

Read on: “for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason”. He was a treasonous negro, and the Most High cannot stand a traitor. He was “fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen”, and “cast out into Egypt.” Imagine being banished, unable to come back to your own country because you were a traitor.

“Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land”, thinking to find succour among the Lacedemonians, where Sparta was. “And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.” What goes around comes around.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:25
precepts.why:
Jason drove many out of their country and perished in a strange land; he cast out many unburied and had none to mourn for him. That is the law Paul states: “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.”

Negroes do evil and think there is not going to be a big payback. You are going to get it. It does not matter that Jason was an Israelite; there is no respect of persons. He slew his own citizens without mercy to please the Greeks, and he received shame for the reward of his treason.

And it was not only Jason. When the king heard of it, he thought Judea had revolted, took the city by force of arms, and there was “killing of young and old”, fourscore thousand destroyed in three days, and no fewer sold as slaves than slain. The Greeks were selling us as slaves long before the slave auctions we know today, and the ones among us who help the enemy against our own people will receive for the wrong they have done.

precepts.label: Psalms 96:5
precepts.why:
The third brother, when they came to cut him, put out his tongue right away and held forth his hands manfully: come on, let's get this over with. He said courageously, “These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.” And “the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man's courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.”

Why did they marvel? They had to understand there was a certain spirit in these brothers; there was something the brothers knew that the king did not. The psalm tells what it is: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols, so the nations have no living God. The king had power, arrogance and the fire, but his gods were dead. These brothers served the Lord that made the heavens, the God who gave them their tongues and hands and would give them again. That is why they were ready to die rather than transgress the laws of their fathers, and why the heathen could only stand there and marvel.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 8:5-6
precepts.why:
The king marveled at the young man's courage, and Paul shows the reason. “For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.”

Because we understand that there is only one living God, that is why they marvel. That is why the king was marveling. The nations have gods many and lords many, but a man who knows the one God, the Father, and the one Lord Jesus Christ can say, “we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.”

Do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. We are already captives: you have bills, you work fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has to be something better. So the brothers went to the fire expecting “the King of the world” to raise them up “unto everlasting life”, and the fourth told the king, “as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

That hope belongs to those who have the one God. What kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God. The one God of Israel will of his own mercy give his servants breath and life again.
